name: ship_3d_object_sprite_project
comment: NAV-DESTINATION PROJECTOR - FULL decode. Loop counter gs:[0x2F77] runs 0x0B-1 down to 0 (11 iterations); entity = 0x6212+((i+0x15)<<5) so entities 0x15..0x1F. GATE: test word [si],0x80 = the entity flags bit7 (active) - inactive entities are skipped. POSITION SOURCE: bx starts at DS:0x4F09 and advances by 6 each iteration (add bx,6 @0x9CF5), i.e. an 11-entry table of THREE int16 (x,y,z), stride 6 - CORRECTION: 0x4F09 is the projector INPUT table, NOT per-frame scratch (0x4F01 is the 8-byte working copy it copies into). Camera origin gs:0x2F65/0x2F67/0x2F69 is subtracted. depth=(x*m[0x18]+y*m[0x1C]+z*m[0x20])>>15, skip if 0, +0x10000 if negative; scale=0x100000/depth -> [bp+0x2A]. screen_x=((x*m[0]+y*m[4]+z*m[8])>>7)/depth+0xA0(160); screen_y=((x*m[0x0C]+y*m[0x10]+z*m[0x14])>>7)/depth+0x64(100). Sprite dims: the far ptr at [si+4] gives w/h, each *scale then shrd 10 (>>10) - matches the port dim*depth_scale>>10. Draw at (screen_x-[si+0xC]/2, screen_y-[si+0xE]/2). BAKED table @file 0x12329 = 11 x (10200,12100,900) IDENTICAL, and the literal 0x4F09 is referenced ONLY here, so the per-destination positions must be written through a POINTER at runtime - locating that writer is the remaining task. PORT GAP: engine.rs render_nav_pyramid_sprites fabricates a 7x4=28-point grid (ROW_Z 600/1500/3000/5600, xi*700, CAMERA_DEPTH_BIAS 8804) - wrong in COUNT (should be 11), GATE (should be entity active bit7) and POSITION SOURCE

name: resource_handle_resolve

name: resource_release

name: resource_free_inner

name: resource_load_by_id

Returns ax=success. THE entry point for loading worlds/scripts: e.g. load venusia = resource_load_by_id(25). Called per-resource by vm_resource_profile_select 0x53da

name: resource_name_lookup
comment: SEG 0x1ce:0x5ea: given DS:SI = FS:0x0c04 name-table entry, resolve/check the resource; returns ebp (0 = skip/already-resolved)

name: resource_file_load

name: resource_file_size

name: resource_load_findfirst_size

name: entity_object_table

Fields observed: +0x00 flags (|0x83 active/type bits, from resource [si]&4), +0x04 data offset + +0x06 data segment (far ptr into a loaded resource segment), +0x0c/+0x0e first two data words (NOT screen position - live gameplay bytes show a far-ptr shape e.g. 0x799a:0x0049; on-screen x/y is DERIVED at draw time from camera/viewport globals 0x277e/0x2780/0x2782/0x2aab/0x2aad + descriptor size, see entity_draw 0x9240), +0x14/+0x16 initial backup of +0xc/+0xe (reset-to values). Populated by entity_object_populate 0x40d0

name: entity_object_populate

First decode of the object-instance system || MERGED 2026-07-25 (audit-fixes #130), also recorded as: ACTIVATES an entity: AX=id DX=resource handle -> di=0x6212+id*32; resolve handle 0x4b9:0x190; flags=([res_hdr]&4)|0x83 (0x80 active bit) at +0; unpack object far ptr +4/+6; copy data +0xc/+0xe; init +0x14/+0x16. THE entity-activation primitive (nav destinations 0x15..0x1F, crew, location content). = 0x299:0x1140

name: entity_object_populate_from_src

Identical record layout (+0x00 flags=([di]&4)|0x83, +0x04/+0x06 unpacked far ptr, +0x0c/+0x0e data words, +0x14/+0x16 init backups) - two independent routines agreeing CONFIRMS the 32-byte entity record structure

name: entity_get_flags

name: entity_flag_state_transition

Per-object flag state machine - entity flags +0x00 bits: 0x80=active, 0x01/0x02 = state (0x83 init = active+state0+bit1). Transitions state0->state-advance

name: entity_flag_toggle_bit6

name: entity_flags_bitmap

name: entity_make_active

name: main_loop_hud_refresh
comment: main-loop per-frame HUD refresh (gated on [0xadf]&1): program VGA sequencer out 0x3c4,ax=0x0f02 (map-mask = all 4 planes), les di,[0x521d] (screen buffer far ptr), clear a 20-byte x 14-row region at row-stride 0x50 (80 bytes/row), then lcall 0x299:0x498 (graphics draw) + lcall 0:0x5d7. CONFIRMS the game renders in mode-X (planar 320x200, 80 bytes/row/plane) via the VGA sequencer, not linear mode 13h. The engine's linear framebuffer produces identical visual output (mode-X is a perf/paging technique, not a visual difference)

name: screen_buffer_far_ptr
comment: far pointer to the mode-X screen/back buffer, used by the HUD refresh (0x1a93) and graphics routines; base for the 80-bytes/row planar layout

name: graphics_plot_modex
comment: SEG 0x299:0x498: mode-X pixel/span plot. Inputs bx=x, dx=y, al=colour. Bounds-check dx vs gs:[0x5239](min+0xa)/[0x523b](max). Address = screen_buffer_far_ptr(gs:0x521d) + y*80 (ax=y<<4 + dx=y<<6) + x/4 (bx>>2); plane = x&3 (cl=bl&3) selected via the VGA map-mask. Confirms mode-X layout: byte offset = y*80 + x/4, plane = x&3. The game's core rendering primitive (my engine's linear y*320+x framebuffer yields the same pixel)

name: screen_clip_bounds
comment: mode-X vertical clip bounds: gs:[0x5239] = height-related min (used as -0xa lower gate), gs:[0x523b] = max y; graphics_plot_modex rejects out-of-range dx

name: dirty_rect_blit
comment: SEG 0x299:0x210d: blit dirty rectangles from the LINEAR back-buffer (gs:0x5229) to the mode-X screen. Gated on dirty flag gs:[0x5231]&1. Per rect record es:[di]: +0x00=x(ax), +0x02=right/x2, +0x04=y(bx), +0x06=width(cx). Source offset = y*320+x (bx*256 via xchg + bx*64 via shl6 = y*320, +x) - the back buffer is LINEAR. Row-skip stride = 0x140-width. KEY: the game renders to a linear back-buffer then dirty-rect-blits to mode-X, so the engine's linear framebuffer matches the game's INTERNAL representation, not just address-equivalent

name: linear_back_buffer
comment: far pointer to the game's LINEAR (y*320+x) back-buffer/composition surface; dirty_rect_blit 0x509d copies rects from here to the mode-X VGA screen. Same layout as the engine's linear framebuffer

name: dirty_flag
comment: back-buffer dirty flag; bit0 gates dirty_rect_blit 0x509d

name: back_buffer_fill
comment: SEG 0x299:region: fill a horizontal band of the LINEAR back-buffer (gs:0x5229) with colour al. di = gs:[0x5239]*320 (top row: cx*256 via xchg + cx*64 via shl6); count = (gs:[0x523b]-gs:[0x5239])*80 dwords (= height*320 bytes); al replicated to eax (ah=al, shl16, ax=bx); rep stosd. Re-confirms the linear y*320 back-buffer layout + gs:0x5239/0x523b as the top/bottom band-row bounds. A screen/band clear before compositing

name: sprite_blit_rle
comment: RLE sprite decode+composite into the LINEAR back-buffer (les di,gs:0x5229). ebp=0xfa00 (64000=320x200 pixel budget). Per token: lodsb control; if negative -> run length cl=(-al+1), sub ebp; lodsb pixel: if 0 -> di+=cx (TRANSPARENT skip) else rep stosb (fill run with pixel); if control>=0 -> literal run (copy cl bytes). So SPR frames are RLE with transparency = index 0, composited into the linear surface (gated on gs:[0x5b57]&1). Matches the engine's SpriteFrameImage transparent-0 model || ALSO RECORDED as `rle_composite_linear_5229`: full-screen RLE compositor into the LINEAR buffer gs:0x5229 - which is a persistent STARFIELD TEXTURE source (NOT the display frame): les di,gs:[0x5229]; ebp=0xfa00 (64000 px); loop reads RLE run bytes from ds:si - negative byte = transparent skip (neg;inc -> cx; add di,cx), positive = opaque run (inc -> cx; rep stosb es:[di],color). PROVES gs:0x5229 is a LINEAR 320x200 row-major back-buffer (di advances 1 byte/pixel, no plane/stride math). Gated on gs:0x5b57 bit0 || MERGED 2026-07-25 (#186): one address, several names, folded by union.

name: main_loop_busy_gate
comment: main-loop idle gate: OR 10 subsystem-active flags ([0x67ac] presentation, [0x24f3],[0x2751],[0x67b0],[0x5e64],[0x2565],[0x2736],[0x2737],[0x27da],[0x2792]); if ANY set, skip the pending-profile dispatch (defer scene load until all idle). Coordinates when a new script profile (dialogue scene / game state) may load

name: main_loop_is_presentation_coordinator
comment: CLARIFICATION: the top-level main loop 0x0FFB is the PRESENTATION/MENU coordinator - input dispatch (0x210e), HUD refresh (0x1a93), per-frame update (0x1fbc, lcall 0x4da:0x204), busy-gate (0x109c), then pending-profile dispatch (0x10c5 -> vm_resource_profile_select). It does NOT run the object-simulation; the entity/object sim + combat run inside game states loaded as script profiles, reached via this loop's profile dispatch - which is why the entity accessors (0x6212 cluster) have no iterator in the main loop

name: vm_exec_loop_dispatch
comment: VM opcode fetch+dispatch: lds si,gs:0x671c (COD script far ptr, or gs:0x677a if resumed); lodsb al = opcode; if 0xff -> end; index bl=al-0xA0 (opcodes are 0xA0-based), bx=index*2; call gs:[bx + 0x6eb0] = opcode handler. Handler table at GS:0x6eb0 (runtime, populated at init). After: repeat/loop via gs:[0x67ab]/[0x67b4] + 0x62b6. A6=idx6, C1=idx0x21, C4=idx0x24, D2=idx0x32

name: vm_opcode_handler_table

name: vm_query_mode_flag

So 'A0 <record-queries> A1' is a conditional block; record ops outside it perform sets. Unifies the whole VM opcode model

name: vm_state_operator_set

comment: entity render (FULL): les di,[0x6212+4] (entity data far ptr); scale bh=(3*[0x2789])/2+1; x=es:[di]*bh>>4 (cx), y=es:[di+2]*bh>>4 (dx); lcall 0x299:0x133d (draw at cx,dx). So the entity's DATA (the .ext-provided object data at record +0x04) is a COORDINATE record: +0x00 = x, +0x02 = y, scaled by the [0x2789] zoom factor. Connects the .ext object data -> entity_object_table -> scaled screen draw. The object-position render path || ALSO RECORDED as `entity_draw`: entity render/process (2 calls): si=0x6212 (entity_object_table); les di,[si+4] (the entity's data far pointer at record +0x04/+0x06); bh=[0x2789]; al=3 (draw mode). Reads a loaded entity's data pointer + renders it - the object-consumer/draw that walks entity_object_table (the per-object draw sought earlier). Connects the object-instance system to the render path || MERGED 2026-07-25 (#186): one address, several names, folded by union.

name: entity_draw_scale
comment: entity draw zoom/scale factor: entity_draw computes bh=(3*[0x2789])/2+1 and scales the object's x/y (from its data record) by bh>>4. A per-view object scale (distance/zoom)

name: resource_switch
comment: resource switch/reload (2 calls): [0xd80]=ax (new id); call close_file_d5b 0xa141 (close current); push cs; call list_d8c_init 0xa757 (reinit the banked list). Switches the active banked resource - close old file + reset the list

name: ems_subsystem_reset
comment: reset the EMS-banked resource subsystem (2 calls): gs:[0xaa0]=0; gs:[0xdba]=0; [0xd9c]=0xffff. Clears the banked-list active/state pointers to their empty values

name: ems_list_query
comment: query the banked list (2 calls): cmp [0xd96],0 (active ptr); cx=[0xd9a] (count); stc. Reads the list's active/count state for iteration/bounds

name: resource_palette_blocks_apply
comment: NAME CORRECTION (was draw_cleanup_set_dirty, which described only the first FIVE instructions and called the whole thing a draw epilogue). THE RESOURCE PALETTE-BLOCK APPLIER: one routine 0xA0C3..0xA116, ret at 0xA116. Prologue: push ax/bx/cx/dx; push ds/push es/pop ds/pop es @0xA0C7 SWAPS ds and es so lodsw reads the caller's stream and rep movsb writes the data segment; dx=si saves the stream start; gs:[0x5b55]=1 marks the screen dirty. LOOP 0xA0D3..0xA0EC: lodsw -> al=start, ah=count; terminator is cmp ax,-1 @0xA0D4, a WORD compare (both bytes 0xFF); di=0x5251+start*3 (bl=3, mul bl); cx=count*3 (mov al,bl / mul bh @0xA0E6); rep movsb copies RAW 6-bit DAC triples into live_palette DS:0x5251. count==0 gives cx=0 and copies ZERO entries, NOT 256. No clamp: start+count>256 would run past the 768-byte buffer. CALLERS 0xA062 (resource_switch) and 0xA780 (list_d8c_init) -- a RESOURCE path, not a draw path, which is what makes the old name wrong. Tail 0xA0EE..0xA115 calls flag_gated_2751 and adjusts gs:0xDAF by the bytes consumed -- NOT read line by line. PORT: src/hnm.rs parse_palette_block

name: queue_d8c_consume
comment: consume a variable-length entry from the gs:0xd8c queue (2 calls): les si,[0xd90] (tail); lodsw ax = entry size; [0xd9a] -= ax (dec remaining count); si += ax (advance past the entry). Dequeues one variable-length record

name: queue_d8c_empty_check
comment: queue empty/full check (2 calls): ax=[0xd8c] head, bx=[0xd90] tail; cmp -> the gs:0xd8c queue is a ring buffer, head vs tail determines empty. Confirms 0xd8c = a variable-length RING-BUFFER QUEUE (head 0xd8c, tail 0xd90, count 0xd9a, wrap [0x5233])

name: queue_d8c_wrap
comment: ring-buffer pointer wrap (2 calls): si += ax; if si > [0x5233] (buffer end) wrap. Handles the gs:0xd8c queue's circular wraparound

name: mode_check_27e0
comment: dual mode-flag check (2 calls): test [0x27e0]&1 AND [0x27e1]&1 -> proceed only if both set. A subsystem-ready gate

name: mem_copy_words
comment: word-block copy (2 calls): rep-style movsw es:[di]<-[si]. Copies N words between buffers

name: queue_d8c_enqueue
comment: enqueue into the gs:0xd8c ring buffer (2 calls): [0xd8c] += ax (advance head), [0xd9a] += ax (add to count); clc. Adds an ax-byte entry to the queue head - the enqueue counterpart to queue_d8c_consume 0xa3d0

name: linear_offset_calc
comment: linear screen offset calc (2 calls): bx*256 (xchg al,ah) + bx*64 (shl bx,6) = bx*320; = the y*320 row-offset into the linear buffer. A coordinate->offset helper

name: snd_play_clip
comment: SND clip player (2 calls): test gs:[0xade]&1 (sound enabled); ds=gs; plays a sound clip (AX=clip index). Matches the prior-session finding (dead_ends): the SND player at 0xb8cd, clip*4 table @DS:0x0BBF, final AX via the lcall [0xcdf] driver callback. The audio playback entry

name: snd_driver_call
comment: SND driver callback invoke (2 calls): ds=gs; lcall [0xcdf] (the registered SND-driver far fn-ptr, per dead_ends sess 001-002 - statically unresolvable). Dispatches to the loaded .drv sound driver

name: ems_resource_flush
comment: EMS-banked resource flush/reload (2 calls): gated on [0xdbc]&1 and file handle [0xd5b]!=0; flushes/reloads the banked resource data. Part of the gs:0xd8c banked-resource management

name: rle_decode_step
comment: RLE decode step (2 calls): ah=0; al=[bx] control byte; if negative (js) it's a run (al+=al, cl=[bx+1] run length). A run-length decompression primitive (same negative-control convention as the sprite blit)

name: timer_tick_b9f
comment: timer/counter tick (2 calls): bl=gs:[0xb9f]; dec; if it underflows call 0xbd26 (reload/fire) else store back. A countdown timer (sound-tempo/frame pacing) that fires 0xbd26 on expiry

name: timer_counter
comment: countdown timer counter (gs:0xb9f); decremented by timer_tick_b9f 0xbd09, fires 0xbd26 + reloads on expiry. A tempo/frame-pacing counter

name: program_pit
comment: PIT RESTORE, not a speed-up (audit-fixes #349 corrects two errors in the previous label). cli; mov al,0x36 / out 0x43,al (channel 0, mode 3 square wave); mov al,0xff then out 0x40,al TWICE -- the raw bytes are `e6 40 e6 40` at 0x07F4/0x07F6, so the port is 0x40 (PIT CHANNEL 0, the system timer), NOT 0x42 (the PC speaker) as this label used to say. Writing 0xFF as both divisor halves gives 0xFFFF, the SLOWEST divisor = the DEFAULT ~18.2Hz -- so this RESTORES the stock tick rate rather than making it faster. Then gs:[0xB21]=0 clears the timer-active flag, sti, and the original INT 08h vector is restored from gs:[0xB1D]/[0xB1F]. The teardown counterpart of 0x079C. src/recomp/io_lift.rs func_7ea had both details right.

name: get_ems_int_vector
comment: startup: int21h ax=0x3567 (get interrupt vector 0x67 = the EMS driver entry); di=0xa. EMS (int 67h) detection/setup - the large-memory banking the gs:0xd8c/ems_paged_read subsystem uses

name: read_cmdline_args
comment: startup: bp=0x23a (PSP/args area); cmp [bp],0; parse command-line arguments (the game needs 'AMR S162227 EMS WRIC:...' launch args, see memory). Reads the invocation config

name: detect_cdrom
comment: startup: ax=0x1500; int 2Fh (MSCDEX/CD-ROM installation check); bx=drive count. Detects the CD-ROM (the game ships on CD)

name: install_ctrl_break_handler
comment: startup: ds=cs; int21h ax=0x2523 (set interrupt vector 0x23 = Ctrl-Break handler) to 0x619. Traps Ctrl-Break so the game cleans up on exit

name: get_video_mode
comment: startup: int 10h ah=0x0f (get current video mode) -> gs:[0x5232]=al. Records the entry video mode for restore on exit

name: dos_dup_handle
comment: DOS file-handle dup (ah=0x45) of the handle at gs:[0xa64] if valid (!=-1). Duplicates a file handle

name: program_sound_port
comment: program a sound-hardware register: dx=gs:[0xa9e] (sound base port); out dx,al. Writes to the sound card's I/O port

name: sound_card_base_port
comment: the sound card's base I/O port (set at init); +6 = status register (polled by 0x0b42/0x0b4e for bit8), written by program_sound_port 0x0c7c. Hardware audio I/O base

name: set_video_mode_saved
comment: restore/set the video mode: al=gs:[0x5232] (the saved entry mode from get_video_mode); int 10h ah=0 (set video mode). Restores the original text mode on exit / sets the saved mode

name: mouse_reset_hide
comment: mouse init: int 33h ax=0 (reset driver), int 33h ax=2 (hide cursor). Initializes the mouse driver with cursor hidden (the game draws its own cursor)

name: mouse_set_hrange
comment: mouse range: cx=ax(min), dx=bx(max); int 33h ax=7 (set horizontal cursor range). Clamps mouse X to the game's coordinate range

name: object_heap_access
comment: runtime object-heap accessor: es=[0x6726] (object heap segment), lds si,[0x672c] (lookup table); di=[si+0x10]; test es:[di],0x118 (object flags). Reads a live object from the runtime heap via the 0x672c lookup - the object-instance heap access (es:0x6726 is the runtime object heap)

name: open_file_c1
comment: resource open: lcall 0x1ce:0x509 (prep); dx=0xc1 (filename in the string seg); ax=0x3d00; int21h (DOS open). Opens a specific resource file (name at gs:0xc1)

name: presentation_state_set
comment: presentation state set: if [0xb13]&2, [0xa32]=1 and [0x2793]|=4 (mark presentation active/pending). Sets the dialogue/presentation-active flags

name: object_heap_segment
comment: segment of the runtime object/instance heap (es:[0x6726]); accessed via the 0x672c lookup table by object_heap_access 0x149b. Holds live object instances (the runtime-gated nav destinations + scene objects)

name: back_buffer_init
comment: back-buffer setup: si=0xea; les di,[0x5229] (linear back-buffer); clear [0x5b53]=0, [0x5b57]=0 (render-ready flags). Initializes the linear composition buffer + its state flags

name: set_screen_page_c000
comment: set the VGA display page: gs:[0x5219]=0xc000 (page offset). Selects the visible VGA page (0xc000 = the high page in mode-X double buffering)

name: presentation_flags_init
comment: presentation state init: al=0x67; [0x67bc]=0x67; [0x67aa]&=0xfc (clear low 2 bits); [0x67ba]=0x67. Resets the dialogue/presentation-ready flags to their armed state

name: state_snapshot_2739
comment: state snapshot/copy: if [0x2739]&1, si=0x161, di=0x270d, movsd copies a state block from 0x161 to 0x270d and increments [0x2738] (a double-buffer/snapshot of presentation state). Gated conditional state save

name: coverage_note_e8_false_positives
comment: NOTE on coverage: the raw E8-relative scan (~360 'near-call targets') includes FALSE POSITIVES - 0xE8 bytes that are operands/data mid-instruction, not real call sites. Verified real function starts are preceded by ret/retf + a clean push prologue. So the true function count is BELOW ~360 and the ~256 labeled fraction is HIGHER than raw-count implies. Label only ret-preceded clean-prologue targets to avoid mislabeling data

name: strlen
comment: null-terminated string length: cx=0xffff; repne scasb (scan es:di for 0); neg cx -> length. Standard C strlen helper

name: file_create
comment: DOS file create: call 0x27c3 (path setup); store gs:[0xa92]=eax; ax=0x3c00; int21h (DOS create/truncate file). Creates a file (temp/save/scratch)

name: file_open_wrapper
comment: file-open wrapper: dx=si (filename); push cs; call path_builder_gs_relative 0x2693; then DOS-open the assembled path. A resource open via the path builder

name: dos_set_drive_and_chdir
comment: DRIVE + DIRECTORY setup, NOT character output (audit-fixes #351 corrects a label that was wrong in its interrupt, its function and its name). Gated on [0x0AE0]&1: `mov ah,0x0E / mov dl,[0x01B9] / int 0x21` @0x27F7..0x27FD is DOS SELECT DEFAULT DRIVE with DL = the drive byte -- the old label read AH=0x0E as a BIOS teletype call and named the wrong interrupt; the instruction here is INT 21h. It then does `mov dx,0x01DA / mov ah,0x3B` @0x27FF, DOS CHDIR to the path at DS:0x01DA. So this is the launch-path setup (cf. the game's `WRIC:\cblood\` argument), not console output.

name: vga_attribute_write
comment: VGA attribute-controller write: dx=0x3c0 (attribute address/data port); al=index (0x31 = palette/overscan), out dx,al then the value. Programs the VGA attribute registers (palette mapping / border colour)

name: linear_to_segment
comment: 32-bit-linear to real-mode segment conversion: shr ecx,4 (linear >> 4 = paragraph); mov ds,cx. Converts a 32-bit linear address into a real-mode segment:offset for banked/large-memory access

name: blood_prng_next
comment: THE PRNG -- this IS 0x01CE:0x0B02 (file = 0x600 + 0x1CE*16 + 0xB02). Hedge removed 2026-07-24: it was labelled a hash/checksum that might be an auxiliary PRNG. AX IN is the MODULUS, AX OUT the value; the 8-round rcr/rcl loop threads a carry through the mixing bytes cs:[0xAF0]/[0xAF1] beside the seed word cs:[0xAEE]. Confirmed three ways: every call site passes a modulus in AX (0x6339 with 5, 0xB8AB with 10, VM 0xA2 at 0x6588), the port ships a faithful implementation of 0x01CE:0x0B02 as ship3d::BloodPrng::next, and 0x2DD3 seeds it from the CMOS RTC seconds

name: gfx_plot_modex_variants
comment: family of clipped mode-X plot/span primitives (0x3106/0x3192/0x3225/0x356e): each clips dx(y) vs gs:[0x523b]/[0x5239] like graphics_plot_modex 0x3428, differing in the shape/vertical offset (sub cx,0xa or 8). The game's set of low-level draw primitives (point/short-span/etc.)

name: gfx_draw_to_page
comment: draw to the VGA display page: les di,gs:[0x5219] (display page ptr); ch=dl; x offset = bx<<4. Renders directly into the visible VGA page (vs the linear back-buffer)

name: order_two_coords
comment: order/sort two coordinate pairs: cmp bx,dx; if out of order xchg dx,bx and bp,cx. Ensures p0<=p1 for a span/line draw (line-clipping min/max helper)

name: full_screen_blit
comment: full-screen copy: les di,gs:[0x5221] (display); cx=0x3e80 (16000); rep movsd (16000 dwords = 64000 bytes = entire 320x200 frame) from si into the display buffer. The full-frame present/copy (whole-screen page copy)

name: composite_draw_a
comment: composite shape draw: call 0x32ac + call gfx_clipped_draw 0x3321 (two plot primitives with xchg bp,dx between). Draws a filled/compound shape from the clipped primitives

name: composite_draw_b
comment: composite shape draw: call 0x39bb + call 0x3ab3. Another filled/compound shape via the plot-primitive family

name: display_buffer_save
comment: display-buffer save/clear: ds=ax; si=0x6612; push [0x5221] (save display ptr); [0x5221]=0. Saves + resets the display buffer pointer (for a page swap/restore)

name: vm_state_record_processor
comment: VM state-record processor: lds si,gs:[0x6724] (object/line-record state table); les di,gs:[0x672c] (lookup); bp=0x24fb (dispatch base); si=gs:[0x6752]. Walks/processes the state records - part of the per-frame VM presentation update

name: index_lookup_dca
comment: index-table lookup: di=0xdca; lodsb al (operand); dec al; cbw (index-1 signed). Indexes a table at DS:0xdca by the script operand

name: fs_name_area_read
comment: read from the FS resource-name area: es=fs; di=0xc74 (near the FS:0x0c04 resource-name table); lodsb - reads a resource name/entry indexed by the script

name: vm_lookup_prep
comment: VM lookup prep (also 0x721a): call table_672c_process 0x604e; si=0x6a16 (the processed lookup output). Prepares the 0x672c->0x6a16 lookup for VM record resolution

name: matrix3d_mul_fixed
comment: fixed-point 3D matrix multiply (family 0x994d/0x9982/0x99a5 = the matrix product rows): imul dword [si+off1] * [si+off2]; sar eax,0xf (Q15 fixed-point >>15); stosd es:[di]. Computes the rotation/projection matrix element products - the ship-3D / object-3D transform math (native counterpart to ship3d.rs build_ship_3d_projection_matrix)

name: angle_wrap_180
comment: ADDRESS CORRECTED 0x97D6 -> 0x97D7 (audit-fixes #386): 0x97D6 is the 0x1E immediate of `add bx,0x1e` @0x97D4, and decoding from it renders the phantom `push ds`. The block starts at the `cmp bx,0x168`. Angle normalization: if bx>=0x168 (360) subtract 360; shr bx,1 (->0..180). Wraps a 0..360 angle into the 0..180 half-range used by the trig/projection tables

name: matrix_table_clear_2a1b
comment: clear the 3D matrix/object table: bp=0x2a1b; cx=6 records; [bp]=0; bp+=0x18 (24-byte stride). Zeros 6x 24-byte records (the per-object transform slots at 0x2a1b)

name: audio_playback_gated
comment: SND/VOC audio playback+mix family (0xbbb3/0xbc50/0xbdb7): gated on gs:[0xade]&1 (sound enabled) and gs:[0xba3]&1; processes/mixes a sound clip into the audio output. The core software audio-mixing routines

name: audio_process_ade
comment: audio processing routine gated on [0xade]&1 (sound) + [0xadf]&1; part of the SND playback path (feeds the driver callback / mixer)

name: ems_map_page_and_copy
comment: EMS PAGE MAP + 16KB COPY, not a DOS IOCTL (audit-fixes #351). `mov ax,0x4400` @0xBD3B looks like the DOS IOCTL function and the old label read it that way -- but the very next instruction is `int 0x67` @0xBD3E, the EMS entry point, so AH=0x44 is the EMS MAP-HANDLE-PAGE function with BX = the handle (from AX) and DX = gs:[0x0A60]. It is followed by `mov cx,0x1000 / rep movsd` @0xBD40, copying 0x1000 dwords = 16384 bytes = EXACTLY one EMS page. The AX value is the same in both APIs; only the interrupt distinguishes them.

name: ems_page_offset_split
comment: EMS address split: cx=ax>>2; ax<<=0xe (14) -> dx. Splits a value into an EMS 16KB-page number + offset (the banked-memory addressing math)

name: ems_buffer_setup
comment: EMS buffer setup: ds=bx; si=0xa6c; [si]=0x4000 (16KB EMS page size); bx=[0xa5e]. Initializes an EMS page-mapped buffer

name: file_read
comment: DOS file read: [0x5b55]=1; cx=2 (or size); ax=0x3f00; bx=di (handle); int21h (read from file into buffer). Reads bytes from an open resource file

name: entity_record_setter
comment: entity record write: ds=gs; si=0x6212 + id<<5 (entity_object_table[id]); writes a field into the 32-byte entity record. Part of the object-instance accessor set

name: entity_flag_accessors
comment: entity flag get/set family (0x41f0/0x426d/0x42ab/0x4374): bx=0x6212 + id<<5; read/modify a flag field (word at gs:[bx] or byte at +offset) of the entity_object_table record. Variants of the entity flag accessors (get_flags 0x41c3 / transition 0x41d1 etc.)

name: range_count
comment: count/length calc: cx = bx - ax + 1 (inclusive range length). A span-length helper

name: resource_get_flags
comment: resource-table flags getter: bx=handle<<3; return ax = fs:[bx+2] (flags word of the 8-byte resource-table entry). Companion to resource_handle_resolve 0x5320

name: resource_get_field4
comment: resource-table +4 getter: bx=handle<<3; return eax = fs:[bx+4] (the dword at +4 of the entry - resource size or data offset)

name: resource_clear_flag
comment: resource-table flag clear: bx=handle<<3; and fs:[bx+2],0xfffd (clear bit1 of the entry flags). Resets a resource-state bit

name: resource_is_loaded
comment: resource loaded-check: bx=handle<<3; test fs:[bx+2] bit0 (loaded flag). Returns whether the resource is currently loaded

name: vm_state_processor
comment: per-run VM state processor (called by vm_run_wrapper 0x55f5): lds si,gs:[0x6724] (state table), les di,gs:[0x672c]+0x10 (lookup); walks the object/line-record state before the exec loop. Prepares/updates the VM state each run

name: camera_fsm_state_gate
comment: camera-approach FSM gate: test [0x27df]&7 (the DS:0x27DF camera-approach phase, ship3d.rs Ship3dCameraApproach); set [0xa32]=1, clear [0x278a]. Gates on the camera state machine phase

name: ui_region_table
comment: table of 8-byte clickable-UI-region records (0x1f entries) at DS:0x65f2; scanned by ui_region_table_scan 0x82c3 for hit-testing (mouse_hit_test 0x8269)

name: project_perspective_x
comment: 3D->2D perspective projection X (family 0x9aa4/0x9c69): sar eax,7 (val>>7); cdq; idiv ecx (divide by depth); add ax,0xa0 (160 = screen centre x). Projects a transformed 3D x coordinate to screen x. The native project_ship_3d_point X (ship3d.rs)

name: project_perspective_y
comment: 3D->2D perspective projection Y (family 0x9ad9/0x9c9e): val>>7 / depth + 0x64 (100 = screen centre y). Projects 3D y to screen y. The native perspective-projection Y

name: draw_vertex_list
comment: vertex-list/polyline draw: lds si,gs:[0x5221] (display); si=[bp] vertex ptr; loop while si!=-1 (0xffff terminator). Draws a 3D polyline/vertex list (the ship-HUD pyramid/route skyline)

name: get_rtc_date
comment: read the real-time clock date: ah=4; int 1Ah (BIOS get RTC date); al=dl; call bcd_to_binary 0x986. Reads + decodes the CMOS RTC date (used for the PRNG seed + any date logic)

name: poll_mouse
comment: poll the mouse: ax=3; int 33h (get position + button status); store gs:[0xa2a]=cx (x), gs:[0xa2c]=dx (y). Reads the mouse cursor position each frame (bx=buttons -> [0xa3e]). Feeds mouse_hit_test 0x8269

name: set_vga_segment
comment: set the VGA video-memory segment: gs:[0x5223]=0xa000 (the VGA graphics segment A000:0). Establishes the base segment for direct VGA writes

name: display_message
comment: display a message string (family 0x0dd8/0x0e08/0x0e36): si=message index (0x73/0x7d/...); lcall 0x299:0x75a (format+render the message). Shows a HUD/status/error message by id

name: ae6_gated_processor
comment: family of routines (0x1344/0x1397/0x13c4) gated on gs:[0xae6]&1 (a mode flag - intro/special state); es=gs then process/copy. Mode-conditional processing

name: resource_close_check
comment: resource-handle close check: cmp gs:[0xa86],0; if a handle is open, close/release it before reuse. Guards resource-handle reuse

name: resource_lookup_helper
comment: resource lookup helper: push cs; call resource_name_lookup 0x28ca; ebp result. Resolves a resource by its name-table entry (used in the load path)

name: fullscreen_op
comment: full-screen (0xfa00=64000-byte) operation: ebp=0xfa00 budget; 32-bit fill/copy loop over the whole 320x200 frame. A screen clear/fill or bulk-decode over the full framebuffer

name: dic_word_lookup
comment: DIC dictionary lookup: lds si,gs:[0x6728] (the DIC far pointer = the text-word dictionary); les di,gs:[0x672c]; si+=ax (word offset). Fetches a dictionary word for 0xA6 TEXT assembly (the b1b2 dictionary-word offsets)

name: scan_zero_word
comment: 0x0000-word-terminated operand scanner: cx=0xffff; loop lodsw until a zero word. This is the length-0 opcode operand-advance (0xA8/0xAC/0xCC/0xD3) documented in dead_ends sess 001 - scans the variable operand to its 0x0000 terminator

name: strlen_b
comment: null-terminated string length (repne scasb variant of strlen 0x2665): cx=0xffff; scan es:di for 0; neg cx = length

name: nav_camera_state_check
comment: per-frame NAV/CAMERA update (gated [0x278B] view-state, [0x278A]&1). Calls object-count gate 0x4DA:0x1E7A; if nonzero runs object_population_loop 0x8D2A -> entity_object_populate 0x40D0, activating the loaded world objects incl. nav destinations 0x15..0x1F. So destinations appear only in the nav view with a world loaded; empty at the console (count 0). Head of the #3/#6 activation chain

name: presentation_mode_check
comment: presentation-mode gate: ax=[0x2793]; and 0xff0f; test 2 -> branch on the presentation-active bit of [0x2793]

name: screen_mode_check
comment: screen-mode gate: test [0x27e2]&2 and [0x5e64]&1 -> branch. Guards a screen/render mode-specific path

name: matrix3d_mul_rows
comment: matrix3d_mul_fixed sibling rows (0x9982/0x99a5/0x99da): same Q15 fixed-point matrix-element products (imul [si+off]*[si+off]; sar 0xf; stosd) as 0x994d - the remaining rotation/projection matrix rows

name: vga_dac_clear
comment: NAME CORRECTED (audit-fixes #412; was gfx_display_draw_family, which described a family this routine is not in). 0x2FA6 is the VGA DAC BLANK: push ax/cx/dx; mov dx,0x3c8; xor al,al; out dx,al (reset the PEL write index); inc dl (-> 0x3c9); mov cx,0x300; then `out dx,al` / `loop 0x2FB4` writing 768 ZERO bytes = all 256 palette entries blanked; pop dx/cx/ax. It contains NO lds/les and never touches gs:[0x5221]. The draw family IS real but starts at 0x2FBB -- 0x2FBB and 0x3000 both open `lds si, ptr gs:[0x5221]` and already carry their own labels blit_page_5221_a/_b. QUERY (0x6E56..0x6E76): di=0x6034(op1) owning object must be ACTIVE (test es:[di+2],1), record's +2 must equal op2, record type must be 0xC2; branch when that fails (0xA1 inverts). SET (0x6E78..0x6E98): owner active, then op2's OWN record needs +2 & 0x20, then vm_special_slot_insert(op2) (0x5FF6, jae=full->exit) and write 0xFFFF into op2+vm_field_offset(0x11,kind). ASYMMETRY: every SET failure path jumps to the RET at 0x6EEC, NEVER to vm_branch - a failed C2 write does not branch. Tail 0x6E9F..0x6EE7 raises a presentation request (kind 2 -> gs:[0x6788]=0x27; kind 0x400 -> DESCRIPT lookup then gs:[0x67AA]|=2 + gs:[0x6788]=0x2B) gated on gs:[0x2793]&1 / gs:[0x67AA]&2 - NOT ported (same engine plumbing the 0xA8 request half needs). Ported: live step() 0xC2 arm || ALSO RECORDED as `vm_op_c2_record_call`: VM opcode 0xC2: les di,gs:[0x6724]; optional 0xA1 skip; lodsw bp; call 0x6034 - object/line-record op with a subcall. Manipulates the runtime state table || ALSO RECORDED as `vm_op_c2_record_state`: 0xC2 line-record state handler; raw token C2 record operand || MERGED 2026-07-25 (#185): one handler under several names.

name: palette_working_buffer_192
comment: 576-byte palette WORKING buffer. 0xB563..0xB56C copies gs:0x5b58 -> gs:0x5851 with cx=0x90 rep movsd = 576 bytes = 192 RGB triples = colors 0..191 ONLY (the live DAC buffer 0x5b58 is 768 bytes / 256 colors). This 0..191 span is exactly why the open audit finding concerns the 128-191 bank: per-screen palette save/restore covers colors 0..191 and leaves 192..255 (the console/text bank) alone. Companion: the panorama frame loader 0x981B refreshes 0x5b58 -> 0x5251 when gs:[0x5B53]&1, and 0xB426 sets [0x5B53]=1/[0x5B57]=1 on ship-3D sequence entry. Port: src/tbbig.rs uses a STATIC GAME_SCREEN_PALETTE_DAC with no refresh-flag model - this working-buffer flow is the unimplemented per-screen palette infrastructure

name: ship_3d_nav_position_table
comment: NAV-DESTINATION POSITION TABLE read by the projector 0x9B98 (bx starts here, add bx,6 per iteration). Entry = three int16 (x,y,z), stride 6. BAKED = 10 identical entries (10200,12100,900) occupying +0x00..+0x3B; the trig table starts at +0x3C. The projector loops ELEVEN times (counter gs:0x2F77 = 0x0B), so its 11th read lands at +0x3C and picks up the trig table's first words (16384,0,16374) - the table is effectively 10 entries and the 11th read OVER-READS (original off-by-one, or entity 0x1F is a never-active sentinel). LIVE-CONFIRMED at boot via re/tools/dump_dosbox_mem.py: records still hold the baked defaults and camera gs:0x2F65 reads (10000,12000,0) = its baked value, i.e. both stay at defaults until ACTIVE navigation. The literal 0x4F09 is referenced ONLY by the projector, so per-destination positions must be written through a pointer during navigation - driving the game there (re/tools/drive_real_game.sh) and re-dumping is the remaining task

name: ship_3d_nav_source_list_build_full
comment: NAV SOURCE-LIST BUILDER (output DS:0x6886, -1 terminated) - FULL decode, PURE RECORD LOGIC (no frontend state, which is what makes the C1 nav-source path portable): lds si,gs:[0x672c] (the 20-byte directory = the DEB records, +0x10 = object offset, +0x12 = entry kind); bx=[si+0x10]; read the object's kind es:[bx]; ax=vm_field_offset(0x11,kind); skip when ax==0 (or ax,ax / je); if es:[bx+ax] == di (the current target) then append [si+0x10] at [bp], bp+=2, and RECURSE depth-first with di = that object. Advance si+=0x14 and continue only while the NEXT entry's +0x12 == 1, else store 0xFFFF and return. Ported: VmMachine::build_nav_source_list (src/vm.rs) || ALSO RECORDED as `ship_3d_navigation_source_list_build`: recursively fills DS:0x6886 with selector-0x11 children of the current target, depth-first, -1 terminated || MERGED 2026-07-25 (#186): one address, several names, folded by union. || DI LIFETIME SETTLED (audit-fixes #194): DI is PRESERVED across the recursion (0x6276 push di / mov di,ax / call 0x624b / 0x627D pop di), so the routine returns the caller's target in DI. This is what lets 0x7259's `mov ax,di` @0x726F be read as the target.

name: ship_3d_object_table_bit_test_full
comment: ALSO RECORDED as `ship_3d_object_table_bit_test`: maps object record to its 20-byte table index and tests high-bit-first bit at selector-5/kind-2 bitset || OBJECT-TABLE BIT TEST - FULL decode. Input ax = an object offset, si = the bitset base record. Scans the gs:0x672c directory comparing ax against each entry's +0x10, counting cx = the DIRECTORY INDEX of that object (di += 0x14 per entry). Then ax = vm_field_offset(selector 5, kind 2) and si += ax = the bitset field; si += index>>3 selects the byte; cl = (index & 7) + 1 and 'shl al,cl' leaves the tested bit in CF, so the bitset is HIGH-BIT-FIRST (index 0 -> bit7, index 7 -> bit0). Returns CF = bit set; the C1 SET caller at 0x6C2F uses 'jb' to take the write path. NOTE the selector/kind are FIXED (5 and 2), not derived from the object || MERGED 2026-07-25 (audit-fixes #184): one address under several names, folded by union.

name: palette_stage_to_dac_copy
comment: PER-SCREEN PALETTE LOADER: si=0x5251 (staging), di=0x5b58 (live DAC buffer), cx=0x90 rep movsd = 576 bytes = 192 RGB triples = colors 0..191 ONLY. Runs on entry to the ship/nav state (immediately after mov [0x24F3],1 @0x8160). Completes the three-buffer flow: gs:0x5251 = per-screen STAGING (filled from the master by the panorama frame loader 0x981B when gs:[0x5B53]&1), gs:0x5b58 = the LIVE 768-byte DAC buffer uploaded by 0x16A7/0x2F90, gs:0x5851 = a 576-byte BACKUP (saved by 0xB563 si=0x5b58->di=0x5851, restored via si=0x5851 @0x1FA1). EVERY copy is 192 colors, so 192..255 (the console/text bank) is never touched by per-screen loading - which is exactly why the open audit finding concerns the 128-191 bank. PORT: src/tbbig.rs renders from a STATIC GAME_SCREEN_PALETTE_DAC and models none of the three buffers or the 0x5B53 refresh flag

name: font_ascii_to_glyph_xlat
comment: 176-byte (0xB0) CP437 -> GLYPH-INDEX translation table -- CORRECTED 2026-07-24 from the earlier 256-byte claim: the table ENDS where the advance table begins at DS:0x78B2 (file 0x14CD2), i.e. 0x14C22..0x14CD2 = 176 entries. Indices >= 0xB0 read into the ADVANCE table, not the map. Extent is pinned by the data: all 176 entries are either 0xff or a valid index into the 86 glyphs, zero out of range. The high half is REAL text data, not padding: 0x81=u-umlaut, 0x82=e-acute, 0x84=a-umlaut, 0x85=a-grave, 0x87=c-cedilla, 0x89=e-diaeresis, 0x8A=e-grave, 0x8B=i-diaeresis, 0x8D=i-grave, 0x94=o-umlaut, 0x95=o-grave, 0x97=u-grave, 0xA8=inverted-question, 0xAD=inverted-exclamation. ORIGINAL NOTE: 256-byte ASCII -> GLYPH-INDEX translation table for the BUILT-IN font, used by render_string 0x31C8 via `xlatb` (bx=0x7802). A result with bit7 set means SKIP the character (`or al,al; js` at 0x31DE). Decoded mapping: 'A'..'Z' -> 0..25, '?'=26, '!'=28, '.'=30, ':'=31, ';'=32, '-'=34, '+'=35, '\'=36
column8: it is NOT folded to uppercase)
column9: '0'..'9' -> 76..85. Space is special-cased BEFORE the xlat (0x31D3 `cmp al
column10: 0x20` -> advance di by 6). Companion tables: per-glyph width byte at DS:0x78B2 (indexed by glyph)
column11: 8-byte glyph bitmaps at DS:0x7908 (glyph<<3). NOTE this is the BUILT-IN font; the console font loaded from HONKF.SPR is a separate asset with its own frame ordering"

name: ship_3d_depth_scale_div
comment: UNSIGNED div: scale = 0x8000000>>7 = 0x100000 divided by the >>15 depth, stored at [bp+0x2A]. Contrast 0x9C6F which divides the SAME depth with a SIGNED idiv -- the projector deliberately treats depth as unsigned for the scale reciprocal and signed for the screen axes, after the 0x9C29 'if negative add 0x10000' fixup

name: ship_3d_screen_axis_idiv
comment: SIGNED idiv (cdq; idiv ecx) of the >>7 dot-product row by depth, then ADD AX,0xA0 (x) / 0x64 (y) for the 320x200 centre. Port project_ship_3d_axis: Rust / on i32 is signed truncating, matching idiv, and the centre add wraps in 16 bits

name: nav_destination_points
comment: NAV-DESTINATION POSITION TABLE - exactly TEN records of three i16 (x,y,z), stride 6, spanning DS:0x4F09..0x4F44. All ten are IDENTICAL: (10200,12100,900). CORRECTION 2026-07-24: the 0x9B98 label previously said '11 x identical' -- it is 10. Offset 60 (DS:0x4F45) is already the ANGLE/TRIG table, so the projector's ELEVENTH iteration reads (16384,0,16374) = the first cosine/sine entries, not a position. Confirmed in the shipped EXE at file 0x12329 AND in live interpreter memory

name: ship_3d_projector_loop_advance
comment: Projector loop tail: pop bx; add bx,6; jmp 0x9BBA. With [0x2F77] seeded 0x0B at 0x9BB4 and DEC/JS at 0x9BBA, the counter takes 0x0A..0x00 = ELEVEN iterations while bx walks 0x4F09+6k for k=0..10. The position table has only TEN entries, so k=10 over-reads into DS:0x4F45. Entity index is 0x6212+((i+0x15)<<5) and i DESCENDS, so the over-read pairs with entity 0x15 (the LOWEST), not the highest. Whether this is intended or an off-by-one is NOT established -- it is moot in every state reached so far because the draw is gated on the entity's active bit7

name: ship_3d_plane_copy_mapmask_all
comment: out 0x3C4, ax=0x0F02 -- VGA SEQUENCER map-mask register (2) = 0x0F, i.e. ALL FOUR planes write-enabled, immediately before the band copy

name: ship_3d_plane_copy_write_mode1
comment: Puts the VGA GRAPHICS CONTROLLER into WRITE MODE 1 (latch copy): out 0x3CE,5 selects the Graphics Mode register, IN AL,0x3CF reads it, AND AL,0xFC / OR AL,1 forces mode 1, and 0xB752 restores the saved value. In write mode 1 each MOVSB copies the 32 bits held in the four plane latches, so one byte moved = FOUR pixels. CONSEQUENCE for the port: combined with the 0x0F map mask at 0xB70E this copy is exactly equivalent to a LINEAR memcpy of 4x the byte count -- the planar layout is a bandwidth technique here, not a visual one, and reproducing it faithfully needs NO planar video model

name: square_caps_char_map
comment: SQUARE-CAPITALS font: 176-byte CP437 -> glyph-index xlat (0xff = no glyph). Selected by the text-measure routine 0x30CD when AX==0 (AX!=0 picks the thin built-in font at DS:0x7802). FOLDS CASE -- 'a' and 'A' both map to glyph 0 -- and carries SPACE as glyph 47, so callers need no upper-casing or space special case

name: square_caps_widths
comment: SQUARE-CAPITALS per-glyph advances, 48 bytes indexed by glyph. Summed by 0x30CD (`add dl,[di+glyph]`) with `sub ax,2` at 0x30FE for the trailing gap. Typical 10, 'I'=3, 'M'=11

name: square_caps_glyphs
comment: SQUARE-CAPITALS glyph bitmaps, file 0x14862. 48 glyphs at a 20-BYTE STRIDE: 8 rows of u16 BIG-ENDIAN followed by 4 zero bytes. This is the face the port previously HARVESTED FROM SCREENSHOTS (25 of 48 cells, one of them -- '4' -- mis-read); it was in the binary all along, reachable from the 0x30CD font selector

name: vm_a6_store_voice_selector
comment: A6 handler: LODSB reads b3 (the voice selector), CBW SIGN-EXTENDS it, and it is stored as a WORD at DS:0x1FAB. 0x11F2 then forms the active line id as [0x1FAB]+9 -> gs:0x6788. NOTE for the port: this makes b3 a LINE IDENTIFIER input, not a one-based talk-clip index -- vm.rs text_selector_voice_clip_index models the latter and is an open suspect

name: vm_a6_accept_clears_active_bit
comment: TEST CL,1 (b4 bit0 = preserve-active): when clear, AND byte [si+1],0x7F clears bit7 of b5 IN THE COD STREAM itself, so an accepted line will not re-display. Self-modifying script data -- the port models it as text_flags_after_accept

name: dlg_line_id_scene_dispatch
comment: SEG 0x971:0. Consumer of the active line id gs:0x6788 (called from 0x1EDD with ax=[0x6788]). Re-reads it at 0x9D1D, rejects negative (js), branches on [0x1FB2]&1 and on specific ids (cmp ax,0x1D at 0x9D2F). The work it does is GRAPHICS, not audio: at 0x9D80..0x9DAA it raises the palette-refresh gates [0x5B53]/[0x5B57] and [0xAE1], loads the buffer far-ptr [0x5229], and calls 0x1ce:0x91d (unpack), then lowers them. TRACED 2026-07-24 with NO sound call on this path || ALSO RECORDED as `render_dispatch_6788`: render dispatch: [0xdb8]=0; ax=[0x6788]; if negative skip; test [0x1fb2],1. Core per-frame render dispatch keyed on the 0x6788 object/scene index (called 8x) || MERGED 2026-07-25 (#186): one address, several names, folded by union.

name: music_voc_name_patcher
comment: Patches the MUSIC filename into the `mu\\xxxxxxxx.voc` template at DS:0x0D2C, writing the 8-char name field at DS:0x0D30. Copies from ds:si uppercasing (cmp al,0x61 / and al,0xDF), stopping at space, control or a high-bit byte; sets gs:0xBA1 if any character CHANGED and gs:0xBA0 if the name was identical, so the caller can skip a reload. RESOLVED 2026-07-24: this is MUSIC, not dialogue voice -- all 44 files in BLOOD.DAT's mu/ are track names (angst, blintr, credits, croolrap, tablo2, generik...) and NONE is a character name. Dialogue voices come from the son.snd bank instead (loader 0xC005, handle DS:0x0C47)

name: vm_a6_selector_b3_store
comment: COMPLETE reference set (2026-07-24, byte-searched): ONE write of the A6 selector b3 (0x668D lodsb / cbw / mov gs:[0x1fab],ax), THREE resets to 0xFFFF (mov word [0x1fab],0xffff at ~0x1A64, 0xB460, 0xB529), and exactly ONE READ -- 0x11F2 `mov ax,[0x1fab]; add ax,9` forming the active line id gs:0x6788. Nothing indexes a sound table from it. So the stored b3 feeds the LINE/SCENE id and nothing else; vm.rs text_selector_voice_clip_index treating b3-1 as a son.snd talk-clip index has no counterpart here

name: chatter_clip_picker
comment: AMBIENT CHATTER voice picker (NOT the dialogue-line voice path). mov ax,0xA; lcall 0x1ce:0xb02 -> prng(10); cmp with the last value at DS:0x0C4D and JE back to the roll, i.e. RE-ROLL UNTIL DIFFERENT; then store it and `add ax,7` so the clip index is prng(10)+7, played via 0xB8CD -> the clip table DS:0x0BBF indexed by clip*4. Gated on [0xCFB]&1 and [0xB2F]==0, which it then sets to 4. The port models this in main.rs (BloodPrng + re-draw-until-different)

name: snd_driver_play_vector
comment: INDIRECT far-call vector for sound playback: every site that plays a clip does `lcall [0x0CDB]` (0xB915, 0xB979, 0xB9D9, 0xBA18, 0xBC47, 0xBCFC). A byte search finds SIX READS AND NO WRITER anywhere in BLOODPRG.EXE, so the vector is filled at runtime by an EXTERNAL SOUND DRIVER -- the game ships driver patterns *MID / *SBP / *GRV at DS:0x023E/0x0248/0x024D. CONSEQUENCE for the port: the trace from a clip index to audible output ENDS at this boundary; what must be faithful is the clip INDEX and the bank layout (table DS:0x0BBF, clip*4 -> {offset,len}), not driver internals. Companion vector DS:0x0CDF (read once at 0xBBA8) is the stop/reset entry

name: dlg_voice_trigger_flag
comment: THE DIALOGUE-VOICE TRIGGER. Complete reference set (byte-searched): SET to 1 at 0x66AF by the A6 handler when it accepts a line (itself gated on gs:0x67B9&1), CLEARED at 0x129C and at 0x94CF (reveal complete), and TESTED at 0xB898 -- the clip picker's gate. One setter, one tester. So an accepted dialogue line is what makes the game play voice, and the clip it plays is prng(10)+7 with no immediate repeat (0xB8AB..0xB8BC). There is NO per-line or per-selector clip choice anywhere in the executable: the A6 selector b3 has exactly one reader (0x11F2) and it forms the line id, and the clip table DS:0x0BBF has only three users (chatter lookup 0xB8F8, player 0xBA22, loader 0xC041)

name: dlg_line_asset_table
comment: PER-LINE ASSET TABLE -- the mechanism behind talk-clip selection. Indexed by the LINE ID (= sign_extend(A6 b3) + 9, formed at 0x11F2) with a 4-BYTE STRIDE; the asset id is the word at entry+2 (0x9D65: mov bx,ax; shl bx,2; add bx,0x1FB5; mov si,[bx+2]). 0xFFFF means NO asset (0x9D71 cmp si,-1). If the id equals the currently loaded one cached at DS:0x1FA3 the reload is SKIPPED (0x9D76); otherwise it is cached and unpacked with the palette gates 0x5B53/0x5B57 raised, buffer far-ptr [0x5229], lcall 0x1ce:0x91d

name: dlg_line_asset_write_cursor
comment: Write cursor for the per-line asset table, seeded at 0x7447: `mov bx,0x1FB5; add bx,0x26; mov [0x1FAF],bx`. 0x26 = 38 is exactly the entry for b3 = 0 -- line id 9, so 9*4 + 2. That pins the indexing: the table is populated from the b3=0 entry upward, so the effective per-line index is b3 ITSELF (0-based), not b3-1. NOTE this contradicts vm.rs text_selector_voice_clip_index, which computes b3-1 AND treats b3=0 as silent

name: dlg_current_asset_id
comment: Currently-loaded per-line asset id; compared at 0x9D76 to skip a redundant unpack, set at 0x9D7C

name: dlg_asset_index_load_and_find
comment: Seeds the per-line asset table's write cursor (mov bx,0x1FB5; add bx,0x26 -> DS:0x1FAF, the b3=0 entry), then loads a NAMED INDEX and searches it. Load: int21 3D00 open, 3F00 read 2 bytes into DS:0x0AAE (the record COUNT), then read count*0x12 bytes into the far buffer at DS:0x0ABC -- so the index is 18-BYTE RECORDS. Search (0x7489..0x74A8): byte-compare each record's name against es:di, `add si,0x12` to step records and `dec [0x0AAE]` to count down; a match falls through to an lseek (int21 4200) using the record's offset, and exhaustion returns AX=0. This is the by-name asset directory the dialogue path resolves through

name: dlg_asset_index_count
comment: Record count of the 18-byte named asset index, read from the file's first 2 bytes at 0x746F and used as the search countdown at 0x74A3

name: dlg_asset_index_buffer
comment: Far pointer to the loaded 18-byte-record named asset index (read target at 0x7481)

name: dlg_line_asset_table_fill
comment: THE FILL for the per-line asset table (completes the chain from A6 b3). di = the cursor gs:[0x1FAF], which 0x7447 seeded at 0x1FB5+0x26 -- i.e. already AT entry+2, exactly where the reader 0x9D6E looks. Per source byte: LODSB + CBW; if NEGATIVE store the sign-extended value unchanged (so 0xFF becomes 0xFFFF, the 'no asset' sentinel the reader tests at 0x9D71); otherwise store (byte-1)*16 (DEC AX; SHL AX,4). Then STOSW + `add di,2` advances a full 4-byte stride to the next entry's +2. The *16 means the stored id is a BYTE OFFSET into a 16-byte-stride NAME TABLE -- the same stride as the sprite filename table at DS:0x0669 -- so a per-line asset is a filename reference, not an ordinal

name: dlg_line_second_cursor
comment: A second write cursor advanced by 0x1A (26) per record at 0x76A2, filled from the same source stream immediately after the asset id at 0x769D. A 26-byte-stride per-line record parallel to the 4-byte asset table

name: dlg_line_record_parser
comment: PER-LINE RECORD PARSER — the source of the per-line asset table. Reads one record from ds:si and fans it into THREE destinations: (1) a NAME copied to DS:0x24C6 (0x766F..0x767E, LODSB with a js/cmp 0x20 terminator like the other name copiers); (2) the ASSET ID at 0x7684, stored as (byte-1)*16 or a sign-extended passthrough, through the cursor DS:0x1FAF into the 4-byte-stride table DS:0x1FB5; (3) a further field at 0x769D through the cursor DS:0x1FAD, which advances 0x1A (26) bytes per record. Immediately preceded at 0x7667 by `mov ax,1; lcall 0xb1b:0x855` — the SND bank loader with AX!=0, the mode that preserves the table and may write son.snd

name: vm_a6_already_shown_gate
comment: TEST word es:[di+2],0x8000 / JNE 0x67A0 -- the per-line ALREADY-SHOWN gate. di = gs:[0x6724] + line_index (0x660D..0x6613), so the flag word lives at the line record +2 and bit 15 suppresses redisplay. Ported as text_line_already_shown / TEXT_LINE_ALREADY_SHOWN_FLAG

name: vm_a6_talk_field_lookup
comment: Computes the TALK field offset the way the game does rather than hardcoding it: AX = 0x13<<4 + 1 = 0x131, then MOV AL,gs:[bx+0x6D60] reads the FIELD-OFFSET MATRIX (selector 0x13, kind slot 1). In the shipped image that byte is 0x3A, which is exactly vm.rs TALK_FIELD. The value is then used as MOV DX,es:[bx+di]; CMP DX,0xC4 (OP_ACTOR) to gate on an active presentation record

name: vm_c4_write_record_entry
comment: THE 3-WORD RECORD WRITE, reached from the 0xC4 handler 0x6C7E after its guard chain 0x6CC3..0x6CFC: MOV word es:[bp],0xC4 (+0 opcode) / MOV word es:[bp+2],bx (+2 related) / MOV word es:[bp+4],0 (+4 zero). The guard-failed path falls to 0x6D13 which calls 0x6462 (vm_branch). Counterpart of vm.rs write_record_entry; the same +0/+2/+4 layout the 0xC9 clear at 0x6FC2 zeroes

name: dlg_record_name_buffer
comment: Name buffer the per-line record parser 0x766F fills (mov di,0x24C6 then a LODSB/STOSB copy). EXACTLY ONE reference in the image -- that write. Nothing reads it by immediate address, so its consumer must receive the pointer; the buffer cannot be traced statically from here

name: fd_path_template_array
comment: `fd\\` path template followed by an ARRAY of 13-byte name slots (12 placeholder chars + NUL): slot 0 at DS:0x0DCA, slot 1 at DS:0x0DD7, stride 13. Slots hold unpatched 'xxxxxxxxxxxx' until a name is written in, the same patch-in-place scheme as mu\\xxxxxxxx.voc at DS:0x0D2C (patcher 0x77A9). LIVE EVIDENCE (runtime_boot DLGTABLE, hub savestate): the per-line asset table DS:0x1FB5 holds 0x0DD7 at +2 for lines 8..23, i.e. a POINTER to slot 1 of this array. fd files are the location BACKGROUNDS (chart.fd, frigo.fd, orx.fd), which fits the 0x9D10 dispatcher doing palette/unpack work

name: vm_opcode_desc_table
comment: THE OPCODE LENGTH/MODE TABLE. 96 two-byte entries for opcodes 0xA0..0xFF, indexed by vm_token_advance 0x62B6 as bp = 0x6F18 + (opcode-0xA0)*2. Entry byte +1 (b1) with bit7 SET marks a sentinel: 0xFF sets mode gs:[0x67AD]=1, 0xFE clears it, 0xFD/0xFB take an optional inline 0xA1 prefix (+1 length). Otherwise the token length is entry[mode] -- b0 in mode 0, b1 in mode 1. DATA-VERIFIED 2026-07-24: byte-identical to vm.rs OPCODE_DESC, all 96 entries, zero mismatches

name: vm_object_directory_far_ptr
comment: Far pointer to the OBJECT DIRECTORY that vm_record_lookup_by_threshold 0x6034 walks: 20-byte (0x14) stride, object NAME at +0x00 and the object's BASE RECORD OFFSET at +0x10, entries in ascending +0x10 order. Live dump (runtime_boot DLGTABLE, hub savestate): names ab/ab/bl/Bo/Bu/Ul/po/Ev (baby1, baby, blood, ..., porte_cles) with bases 0, 0x14, 0x28, 0x4A, 0x92, 0xDA, 0x122, 0x16A. 0x6034 returns the greatest base STRICTLY LESS THAN its AX input -- i.e. which object OWNS a given record offset. Ported as ExecutionContext::owner_object_offset

name: vm_post_update_c4_pair
comment: POST-UPDATE actor-pair step. CMP AX,0xC4 gates on an actor record; reads the record's THIRD word ds:[bp+4] and proceeds only when it is ZERO and gs:0x67B6 bit0 is CLEAR (0x5D9A..0x5DA6), then NOT AX / MOV ds:[bp+4],AX writes 0xFFFF as a PROCESSED MARKER (0x5DAA..0x5DAC) so the pair is handled once. Follows ds:[bp+2] to the related record (di); the 0x5DB0..0x5E06 block is SYMMETRIC -- whichever of {owner si, related di} has kind 1, the OTHER partner's selector-8 ENCOUNTER COUNTER is INCd (resolved against that other partner's kind, so kind 2 / offset 0x36), bit15 of the OWNER's [si+2] is set, gs:0x6798 = the bumped record and vm_cod_scan 0x739B runs. Both paths then fall to 0x5E09's C4 write. Port: vm.rs post_update_execution_state + post_update_encounter_counter -- VM_PRESENTATION_PAIR_WRITE_DISABLED = 0x67B6 confirmed here || MERGED 2026-07-25 (audit-fixes #130), also recorded as: post-update C4 pair path: marks primary aux 0xffff and writes reciprocal selector-0x13 C4 record

name: vm_post_update_c6_branch
comment: POST-UPDATE branch for 0xC6 records (inside OP_RECORD_ENTRY_MIN..MAX = 0xC5..0xC8). A small state machine over gs:0x2792 (phase counter), gs:0x2A7B and gs:0x278B: phase 0 with [0x2A7B]==1 bumps the phase, sets [0x278B]=8 and calls 0x299:0x1241 with AX=4; the next pass (phase 1, [0x278B] cleared) bumps again, clears [0x2A7B]/[0x278A] and writes gs:[0x6788] = 0x2C -- i.e. it TRIGGERS A SPECIFIC LINE by setting the active line id directly, the same variable the A6 handler forms from b3+9. Falls through to a gs:0x1FB2 test at 0x5E7E, the gate vm.rs models as C2_PRESENTATION_GATE

name: vm_query_set_mode_flag
comment: The VM query/set MODE flag (0 = mode 0, 1 = mode 1). SEVEN writers, enumerated by byte search 2026-07-24: 0x62DD sets 1 and 0x62EC sets 0 from the OPCODE_DESC sentinels 0xFF/0xFE in vm_token_advance; 0x6473 resets it to 0 inside vm_branch; 0x6559 is the 0xA0 PUSH handler (set 1) and 0x6572 the 0xA1 POP handler (set 0); 0x6839 sets 1 inside the 0xA9 handler; and 0x540D writes it from AL in the record ladder. IMPORTANT for the port: vm.rs walk is a STATIC decoder and tracks only the two SENTINEL writers, so its mode can diverge from the runtime value after a branch or an A9 -- and token LENGTH is mode-dependent, so a wrong mode desyncs the walk

name: vm_c1_write_record
comment: 0xC1 record write: MOV word es:[bp],0xC1 / MOV AX,gs:[0x6736] / MOV es:[bp+2],AX / MOV word es:[bp+4],2. Note TWO differences from the C4..C8 writers -- the related word comes from the stored operand gs:0x6736 rather than BX, and the third word is 2, not 0. Ported as vm.rs write_c1_record_state_mode0

name: vm_c3_write_record_link
comment: 0xC3 record-LINK write: MOV word es:[bp],0xC3 / MOV es:[bp+2],BX / MOV word es:[bp+4],1. The third word is 1, unlike the 0 that C4..C8 write. Ported as vm.rs write_record_link -- a separate function precisely because of this

name: vm_field_selector_05
comment: Field selector 0x05 -- defined for KIND 1 ONLY, offset 0x1E. Used at 0x60A8: `add si,ax` then `mov cx,0xA; xor bx,bx; lodsw...` -- it addresses the base of a TEN-WORD ARRAY that is iterated. Not modelled in the port

name: vm_field_selector_08
comment: Field selector 0x08 = the ENCOUNTER COUNTER -- KIND 2 ONLY, offset 0x36. CORRECTION: the row is `00 36 00 ...` and vm_field_offset's BSF makes column 1 the kind whose lowest set bit is bit1, i.e. kind VALUE 2 (an earlier note here read the column index as the kind and called it kind 1). Both readers agree: 0x83D4 gates `cmp word [si],2` and 0x91CE `test word [si],2`. Used twice in the post-update ladder (0x5DC4 resolving the RELATED kind then `inc [eax+edi]`, 0x5DEC resolving the OWNER kind then `inc [eax+esi]`): whichever partner is kind 1, the OTHER (kind-2) partner's counter is bumped, then `or word [si+2],0x8000` sets bit15 on the OWNER's +2. PORTED: vm.rs post_update_encounter_counter + the two filters (source_list_display_rows / source_list_text_rows)

name: vm_field_selector_0d
comment: Field selector 0x0D -- KIND 8 ONLY, offset 0x16. Used at 0x5ED9 in the 0xC6 post-update branch: `mov dx,[eax+edi]` reads it, immediately followed by resolving selector 0x0A -- the two are used as a pair. Not modelled in the port

name: vm_field_selector_0f
comment: Field selector 0x0F -- KIND 1 ONLY, offset 0x46. Used at 0x5720: resolve, `add ax,di`, `mov ax,es:[bx]`, `or ax,ax` -- a field READ with a zero test gating what follows. Not modelled in the port

name: vm_field_selector_00_flags
comment: Field selector 0x00 resolves to offset 0x02 for EVERY kind (0..10) -- the per-record FLAGS/ACTIVE word. This is what makes the port's hardcoded `state[owner+2] & 1` active test safe: it is a matrix INVARIANT, not a kind-1 assumption. Contrast selector 0x11 (LOCATION_FIELD), which varies 0x06/0x18/0x16/0x14/0x04 by kind and where hardcoding IS an assumption

name: vm_field_offset
comment: FIELD-OFFSET RESOLVER, fully decoded: SHL AX,4 (selector*16) then BSF BX,BX -- BIT SCAN FORWARD on the kind -- then ADD BX,AX and MOV AL,gs:[bx+0x6D60]. So the KIND IS A BITMASK and the matrix column is the index of its LOWEST SET BIT, not the kind value: column k corresponds to kind value 2^k (column 8 = kind 0x100). vm.rs vm_field_offset models this exactly with kind.trailing_zeros(), and its `if kind == 0 { None }` guard matches BSF leaving the destination undefined for a zero source || MERGED 2026-07-25 (audit-fixes #130), also recorded as: helper: returns GS:0x6D60[selector*16 + bsf(kind)] as a kind-specific record-field offset

name: vm_list_filter_on_seen_counter
comment: List filter: `cmp word [si+0x36],0 / je skip` then `cmp [si+0x18],bx / je skip`. +0x36 is the selector-8 ENCOUNTER COUNTER and +0x18 the selector-0x11 LOCATION field -- both KIND-2 columns (FIELD_OFFSETS[8][1]=0x36, FIELD_OFFSETS[0x11][1]=0x18), matching this loop's `cmp word [si],2`. bx = gs:0x6758 = the built-in object Ark, so an object is included only when its counter is NONZERO and it is NOT aboard the Ark. Composer: the status text block at 0xE18 (PLANET:/SHIP:/BLACK HOLE: header from DS:0x12E/0x137/0x13E + the location name, then LIFE SUPPORT: DS:0x14B and this roster, UNKNOWN DS:0x16C when empty). PORTED: vm.rs source_list_text_rows

name: vm_list_draw_filter_on_seen_counter
comment: List DRAW loop: `cmp word [si+0x36],0 / je next` skips objects whose selector-8 counter is zero, else `add si,4`, `lcall 0x299:0x202` (draw) and `add dx,0xA` to step one row. So the counter incremented by the post-update ladder at 0x5DCE/0x5DF6 decides whether an object APPEARS IN A DISPLAYED LIST. The counter is a KIND-2 field (FIELD_OFFSETS[8][1]=0x36), consistent with this loop's `test word [si],2`. PORTED: vm.rs source_list_display_rows

name: vm_source_list_draw_loop
comment: SOURCE-LIST DRAW LOOP over gs:0x6886 (the list 0x4DA:0xEAB builds, i.e. the 0x624B nav-source build). Walks word entries until the 0xFFFF terminator and applies THREE filters before drawing each: (1) `test word [si],2` -- the object's kind must have bit 1 set; (2) `test word [si+2],1` -- the ACTIVE bit; (3) `cmp word [si+0x36],0` -- the selector-8 SEEN COUNTER must be non-zero. Survivors get `add si,4`, `lcall 0x299:0x202` (draw) and `add dx,0xA` for the next row. The port builds this list (VmMachine::build_nav_source_list) but the three draw-time filters live in the CONSUMER, which is where the counter filter is missing

name: ship_3d_plot_point
comment: Point-cloud PLOT. Signed clip against DS:0x5235/0x5237 (x) and DS:0x5239/0x523B (y) with JL/JGE. Address = y*320 built as XCHG BH,BL (y*256) + SHL DI,6 (y*64), then + x. OCCLUSION: MOV AL,es:[di] / OR AL,AL / JNE -- a point is written ONLY where the pixel is still zero, so nearer points drawn first win. Shade = 0xEF - (depth >> 12) via SHR AX,0xC / NEG AL / ADD AL,0xEF. Ported exactly as ship3d.rs plot_ship_3d_projected_point + ship_3d_projected_point_shade/offset || ALSO RECORDED as `ship_3d_projected_point_plot`: clips projected point against DS:0x5235..0x523B and writes depth shade into ES framebuffer if empty || MERGED 2026-07-25 (#186): one address, several names, folded by union.

name: ship_3d_point_cloud_table
comment: POINT-CLOUD table for the starfield: 1000 records (cx = 0x3E8 at 0x9A1D) of EIGHT bytes each, read as two LODSD per iteration at 0x9A34 into the scratch di[0]/di[4]. LAYOUT IDENTITY: 0x2FC1 + 1000*8 = 0x4F01, exactly the scratch buffer address the same projector uses -- so the table occupies DS:0x2FC1..0x4F01 with no gap. Each record's first three words are x/y/z (camera origin DS:0x2F65/67/69 is subtracted at 0x9A3F..0x9A47); the fourth word is not used by the projector

name: vm_handler_table
comment: VM opcode HANDLER table, indexed by vm_dispatch 0x5627 as `call gs:[bx+0x6EB0]` with bx=(opcode-0xA0)*2. LAYOUT IDENTITY fixes its extent: 0x6EB0..0x6F18 (where OPCODE_DESC begins) is 104 bytes = 52 entries, i.e. opcodes 0xA0..0xD3 -- and the last entry (0xD3) is NULL (0x0000), so the highest dispatched opcode is 0xD2 (its handler offset 0x1118 corresponds to file 0x64B8, the script-profile request). CONSEQUENCE: the VM executes only 0xA0..0xD2, while OPCODE_DESC describes 96 opcodes 0xA0..0xFF -- the remaining 45 entries exist purely so the token walker can compute LENGTHS for non-executable data tokens

name: vm_entity_table
comment: Entity records, 32 bytes each. LAYOUT IDENTITY bounds the count: 0x6212 + 32*32 = 0x6612, exactly the dirty-rect list, so there are exactly 32 entities (0x00..0x1F). That is why the nav projector 0x9B98 iterates the LAST ELEVEN (0x15..0x1F)

name: ship_3d_hud_pyramid_vertices
comment: 32 pyramid HUD vertices, (x,y,z) i16, stride 6. DELIBERATE ALIAS, confirmed by probe: these 192 bytes are ALSO palette colours 192..255 of the DAC buffer at DS:0x5B58 (0x5B58 + 576 = 0x5D98), and the game uses both readings -- 0x2F90 uploads all 768 bytes to the DAC while the HUD projector reads the same bytes as vertices. A live dump shows 192/192 bytes unchanged from the image, so the range is never overwritten. Grouped by 2 they are vertices; grouped by 3 they are colours. Both port constants (SHIP_3D_HUD_PYRAMID_VERTICES and GAME_SCREEN_PALETTE_DAC[576..768]) are correct

name: nav_status_hover_composer
comment: NAV-CHART HOVER STATUS PANEL (entry 0x82E8 = nav_state_gate; composer 0x8347..0x8420). Gated by three flags ([0x27DA],[0x278A],[0x67AC] bit0) then a MOUSE HIT-TEST of [0xA2A]/[0xA2C] against the widget rect at DS:0x65F2+8 -> [0x27E2] |= 1. Composes a CR-separated, NUL-terminated text block at 0xE18: header DS:0x12E `PLANET: ` / DS:0x137 `SHIP: ` (kind==0x10) / DS:0x13E `BLACK HOLE: ` (kind&0x100) chosen from the CURRENT LOCATION object fs:[arche+0x16]; then that object's INLINE NAME at +4; then DS:0x14B `LIFE SUPPORT:`; then the roster (0x624B source list filtered by 0x83D4..0x83E8). PORTED: vm.rs location_status_block

name: dead_unknown_fallback
comment: DEAD CODE: the `UNKNOWN` (DS:0x16C) fallback of the status composer. 0x83FD is an UNCONDITIONAL `jmp 0x840E` that skips it, and a whole-image relative-branch scan (re/tools/find_jump_target.py 0x83FF) finds ZERO branches to 0x83FF; `be 6c 01` (mov si,0x16C) occurs exactly once, here. So the shipped composer never emits UNKNOWN -- do not port it

name: nav_hover_widget_descriptor
comment: widget descriptor the status-hover gate reads: +0 byte flags (bit0 must be set, 0x830D), +8 the hit-test RECT as x,w,y,h words (0x8318..0x832D compares against mouse [0xA2A]/[0xA2C])

name: object_inline_name
comment: An object record's NAME, NUL-terminated, stored INLINE at record+4. Read by both list consumers (0x8389/0x83EA `add si,4` + lodsb; 0x91E1 `add si,4` before the 0x299:0x202 draw). Verified against shipped data by re/tools/check_object_inline_names.py: 630/640 kind-1 objects in SCRIPT1..5 hold exactly their DEB name; the 10 exceptions are `blood` and `orxx` in each script, the built-ins whose record bytes the engine reuses. PORTED: vm.rs object_inline_name

name: location_info_panel
comment: ADDRESS CORRECTED 0x9100 -> 0x90FF (audit-fixes #387): 0x9100 sat inside the 4-byte `inc byte [0x2789]` at 0x90FF, and 0x2789 is the very scale variable this label names. DESTINATION INFO PANEL + its zoom FSM (state gs:0x2788, scale gs:0x2789). Opened by the selection commit 0x8FF4..0x905B (writes gs:0x27BF = the picked object, REFUSING the object you are already at via `cmp ax,es:[arche+0x16]` @0x901D; seeds the 4x4 cursor rect at gs:0x2AAB = {mouse x, mouse y, 4, 4}; [0xADA]=8 steps, [0xADB]=0; [0x2788]=1; [0x2789]=0; disables the mouse [0xA3E]=0). STATE 1 = zoom OPEN: each frame entity_draw_full + interpolate the cursor rect toward the panel rect (0x8B:0xFAD = ship_3d_interpolation_gate, which DRAWS the interpolated rect rather than storing it), CF set when done -> [0x2788]=0. STATE 0 = open: draws the window blit (0x299:0x40E with the four words at DS:0x2780 and the source handle [0xAC8]) then the text; re-enabling the mouse ([0xA3E]&1 @0x912E) starts the close. STATE 2 = zoom SHUT (0x91F1): dec [0x2789], interpolate back, then [0x2788]=0, [0x27BF]=0, [0x676A]=0. TEXT PORTED: vm.rs location_panel_rows

name: location_info_panel_rect
comment: the info panel's box rect, a STATIC constant (no writer anywhere in the image; the only references are the two `mov si/di,0x2780` at 0x9114/0x9203 and the draw at 0x9142): x=0x64 y=0x14 w=0xA0 h=0x46 = (100,20,160,70). The panel text at x=0x6E y=0x19 and pitch 0xA fits five roster rows inside it (y=45..85)

name: location_info_panel_cursor_rect
comment: the info panel's zoom SOURCE rect, written at 0x9029 as {mouse x [0xA2A], mouse y [0xA2C], 4, 4} -- the panel zooms open from a 4x4 square at the cursor

name: window_blit_entry
comment: ALSO RECORDED as `blit_coord_guard`: blit coordinate guard: or dx,dx; je/js skip (reject zero-or-negative coordinate); or bp,bp. Entry guard shared by the clipped-blit family (also at 0x3b85, 0x3c6c) that culls off-screen/degenerate spans before drawing || the clipped blit the panel's window chrome goes through (0x299:0x40E; bx=x cx=y dx=w bp=h si=[0xAC8]=0x5F11 the source handle). Shares the blit_coord_guard prologue. UNDECODED: what [0xAC8] resolves to -- the port draws the panel TEXT (vm.rs location_panel_rows) but not yet its chrome || MERGED 2026-07-25 (audit-fixes #184): one address under several names, folded by union.

name: render_string_entry
comment: STRING DRAW entry (0x299:0x202): zeroes gs:0x27CD, clips, then runs render_string 0x31C8. gs:0x27CD accumulates the drawn width -- but ONLY over glyphs (`add word gs:[0x27cd],ax` @0x3215). The SPACE path (`add di,6 / jmp` @0x31D7) moves the pen WITHOUT touching it, and unmapped bytes are skipped entirely, so the reported width is not the pen distance. Ported: font.rs game_font_drawn_width || NARROWER EARLIER READING `clipped_blit_w8_a`: clipped blit: cmp dx,gs:[0x523b] (clip Y to screen height); reject if below; cx=gs:[0x5239]-8 (clip X to width, 8-px span). Bounds-checked span copy into the display page || MERGED 2026-07-25 (audit-fixes #133): one address, two names, the shorter describing a prologue or a single facet. Kept because a narrow reading records a true observation; renamed away because it is not what the routine IS.

name: palette_blend_remap_table_build
comment: CORRECTED (was abs_negate_gs_setup, which only described the first four instructions). THE TINT REMAP-TABLE BUILDER, far-called as 0x1CE:0x0000 with DI = a 256-byte destination table, AX = the NEGATED blend percent, BX/CX/DX = the target colour. Prescales the target (pct*comp/100, three pushes at 0x22F5/0x22FD/0x2304) and the source weight (100-pct @0x230D); then for each of the 256 entries of the LIVE palette at DS:0x5251 computes blended = src*(100-pct)/100 + target*pct/100 and NEAREST-SEARCHES all 256 entries by squared RGB distance (0x2366..0x238E), seed distance 0xBB8 and `ja` on strictly-greater so TIES TAKE THE LATER index; a source with no match within 0xBB8 leaves its table byte UNCHANGED (`js 0x23B0` skips the store). This is how every translucent/tinted overlay in the game is drawn. PORTED: palette.rs build_palette_blend_remap_table || SUPERSEDED READING `abs_negate_gs_setup`: abs/negate helper: bp=gs; ds=es=gs; si=dx; neg ax. Rebases segments to the work arena and negates/absolutes the ax argument (called 5x) || MERGED 2026-07-25 (audit-fixes #131): the superseded rows were left in the file beside their own correction, so a reader who found one had no pointer to the other.

name: tint_remap_table_a
comment: 256-byte tint remap table (runtime-built; all-zero in the image). Its twin is DS:0x6011 -- LAYOUT IDENTITY 0x5F11 + 0x100 = 0x6011 -- and 0x45C8 picks between them by a mode byte, storing the choice at gs:0x524B. Readers xlatb through it (0x3283 `mov dl,gs:[edx+0x5F11]`, 0x3416 in the rect blit). The destination info panel fills 0x5F11 at 0x90F6 with 50% toward black

name: live_palette
comment: the LIVE palette (768 bytes, 6-bit DAC units, 3 bytes/entry) the tint-table builder nearest-searches (0x2354). Runtime state -- all-zero in the image. Distinct from the boot palette buffer DS:0x5B58 (file 0x12F78) the port bakes as GAME_SCREEN_PALETTE_DAC

name: tint_rect_inner_loop
comment: the `box draw` is NOT a blit: al = es:[di] (the pixel ALREADY on screen), xlatb through the table at BX=SI, stosb. So 0x299:0x40E with si=[0xAC8] REMAPS the rect in place -- a translucent window. Row stride bp = 0x140 - width. PORTED: sprite.rs remap_rect_indexed

name: nav_chart_object_pick
comment: NAV-CHART OBJECT PICKER: walks the visible-object list at DS:0x2AD3 ([0x27C1] entries) and hit-tests each marker. Marker position = the object's selector-0x0B field (FIELD_OFFSETS[0x0B] = 0x18 for kinds 8 and 0x10): x at +0x18, y at +0x1A. Box size BY KIND: default (0x0C,0x0B); kind&0x100 BLACK HOLE (0x13,0x0C); kind&0x10 SHIP (0x15,0x0A). A black hole has TWO chart positions -- +0x18/+0x1A and +0x1C/+0x1E -- and uses the second when es:[obj+0x14] != es:[arche+0x22] (0x92DF..0x92F2), i.e. the two ends of the same wormhole. Box origin is (x-2,y-2) and both bounds are INCLUSIVE (jb/ja). Returns the FIRST hit in list order, else 0. Caller 0x8FB0: with the mouse ENABLED the hit becomes the info-panel selection (0x8FF4), with it disabled the object's name is drawn as a hover label. PORTED: vm.rs nav_chart_pick

name: nav_chart_visible_object_list
comment: the nav chart's visible-object list, [0x27C1] word entries, walked by the picker 0x92A3. Runtime state

name: world_art_table
comment: WORLD-ARTWORK table: 42 records of 0x16 bytes, +0x00 a 16-byte NUL-terminated DISPLAY NAME, +0x10 a RESOURCE ID into the filename table at file 0xCDF4, +0x12 a group word (31 for every entry), +0x14 zero. Walked by the info panel's first zoom frame (0x9098..0x90B6: compare each name against the selected object's inline name via 0x1CE:0x2C4; on a match load [si+0x10]|0x8000 as a resource at 0x90B8..0x90C3). LAYOUT IDENTITY: 0x2BC7 + 42*0x16 = 0x2F63, two bytes before the nav camera origin DS:0x2F65. Display names are NOT asset names -- Oddland=trou.ext, Bonus=forest.ext, Troma=glacia.ext, Trashlando shares kortex.ext -- which is why this table must be read, not inferred. All 42 ids resolve to real filename records (re/tools/dump_world_art_table.py). PORTED: levels.rs WORLD_ART_DIRECTORY + parse_world_art_table

name: location_info_panel_dispatch
comment: the info panel's per-frame DISPATCH: es=gs; `test byte [0x2788],1 / je 0x9125` selects zoom-open vs the rest; within zoom-open `cmp [0x2789],0 / jne 0x90FE` runs the ONE-TIME setup only on the first frame (resolve the object's artwork through DS:0x2BC7, load it, position entity 0 at the cursor, and stash the scaled width at [0x277E]). PORTED: engine.rs LocationPanelState + step_location_info_panel

name: nav_chart_list_build
comment: NAV-CHART VISIBLE-OBJECT LIST builder (far 0x4DA:0x1E7A; output DS:0x2AD3, count returned in AX and stored at [0x27C1] by 0x8D2A). Calls 0x604E to build the active-object candidate list at DS:0x6A16, then walks it (terminator = a NEGATIVE word) and keeps every object whose KIND word has any of the bits 0x118 -- kind 0x08, kind 0x10 (SHIP), kind 0x100 (BLACK HOLE). Stores the terminator and returns the count. PORTED: vm.rs build_nav_chart_list || NARROWER EARLIER READING `vm_helper_604e`: VM helper: eax=0; cx=ax; call 0x604e (VM lookup-prep sibling of 0x71cf). Zeroes accumulators then runs the record-resolution prep || MERGED 2026-07-25 (audit-fixes #133): one address, two names, the shorter describing a prologue or a single facet. Kept because a narrow reading records a true observation; renamed away because it is not what the routine IS.

name: active_object_list_build
comment: ACTIVE-OBJECT candidate list (output DS:0x6A16, 0xFFFF-terminated): walks the 20-byte directory gs:0x672C while +0x12 == 1 (STOPS at the first entry that is not, it does not skip), takes each object offset [si+0x10] and keeps it when fs:[obj+2] & 2 -- the IN-PLAY bit the story sets. Consumers: 0x721A (the nav chart) and the 2nd caller. PORTED: vm.rs build_active_object_list || ALSO RECORDED as `table_672c_process`: processes the 20-byte lookup table (2 calls): es=gs; di=0x6a16; lds si,gs:[0x672c] (the vm_lookup_table_20b); copies/transforms entries into 0x6a16. Prepares the 0x672c lookup data || MERGED 2026-07-25 (#186): one address, several names, folded by union.

name: nav_choice_dispatch
comment: NAV-CHOICE DISPATCHER: gated on [0x2793]&8, takes the committed choice [0x2A19], `dec bx / add bx,bx` to make it a 0-based word index, tests the phase byte [0x2565]&1 and then `call word ptr cs:[bx+0xF29]` -- the 5-entry near-offset table at 0x8709 (0F33 0F4C 0FDD 1068 108C). CS base = 0x8709-0xF29 = file 0x77E0, so the five handlers are file 0x8713, 0x872C, 0x87BD, 0x8848, 0x886C (confirmed: 0x0F4C -> 0x872C = the already-labelled nav_choice_handler_1). PORTED: ship3d.rs run_ship_3d_nav_choice_handler_0..4

name: nav_choice_handler_3
comment: navigation-choice handler 3 (dispatch-table entry 3). PORTED: ship3d.rs run_ship_3d_nav_choice_handler_3 || MERGED 2026-07-25 (audit-fixes #130), also recorded as: static C3 record-link handler: DS:0x6756 -> DS:0x676A, clears phase, reloads radio.snd

name: save_writes_current_profile
comment: SAVE/LOAD PROFILE ASYMMETRY, deliberate: the writer streams 2 bytes from DS:0x677E (vm_resource_profile_index -- the CURRENTLY selected profile) at 0x1C63, but the reader at 0x1CEB streams them into DS:0x6780 (vm_pending_resource_profile -- the slot the 0xD2 opcode posts REQUESTS into). So loading a save does not switch script sets itself; it posts the saved profile as pending and the main loop's normal dispatch (0x108E -> 0x10C5) performs the switch on the next pass. The other two blocks are symmetric: 0x200 bytes from DS:0x6ADE (0x1C6D) and 0x60 bytes from DS:0x6CDE (0x1C72). src/bloodsav.rs previously documented [0x6780] for BOTH, which hides the mechanism

name: list_widget_box_is_a_tint
comment: THE CONSOLE CHOICE BOX IS NOT PAINTED, IT IS TINTED: after computing the rect (0x84A1..0x84C3 -> DS:0x2AAB x,y,w,h), the widget does `mov si,[0xAC8]` (= 0x5F11, the 50%-toward-black remap table built by 0x22E0) and `lcall 0x299:0x40E` -- the same translucent-window primitive the destination info panel uses. There is NO border/fill colour pair. The [0x27E6]&1 branch at 0x84CD is a QUERY-ONLY early return (0x85D3 returns [0x27E7]-1), not an alternate draw. Label colours ARE immediates: `mov al,0xE8` @0x8565 (unselected), `mov al,0xEF` @0x858B (selected), overridden to `mov al,0xFE` @0x8595 when the mouse is enabled (test byte gs:[0xA3E],1 @0x858D). name: save_slot_edit_begin
comment: SAVE-SLOT RENAME entry: [0x2734] = 0x25ED (the slot record being renamed), [0x2732]=0, then `rep movsd cx=4` copies that record's 16 name bytes into the EDIT BUFFER DS:0x273B (0x1BBD); [0xADA]=6 (interpolation steps), [0xADB]=0, [0x27E6]=0, [0xADC]=0. The widget then substitutes the buffer for that row as it draws (0x8573 `cmp si,[0x2734] / jne / mov si,0x273B`).
