name: montage_frame_setup
comment: MONTAGE/CINEMATIC PER-FRAME SETUP, and the consumer of the SECOND tint table: bx=0 cx=0 dx=0x140 bp=0xC8 si=DS:0x6011 then `lcall 0x299:0x40E` -- remaps the WHOLE 320x200 screen through tint table 0x6011 (the twin of 0x5F11; 0x45C8 selects between them into gs:0x524B). Then ax=0, bp=0x8C, cx=0 and `lcall 0x299:0xCDC` draws a (0,0,*,140) region -- the FILM area only, rows 0..140. Finally the two far pointers [0x5221]/[0x5229] are swapped (page flip). This is why the console band at rows 140..200 persists across the montage: the per-frame work never touches it. NOT YET PORTED: engine.rs overlays a harvested band instead, and does no full-screen remap

name: tint_table_build_banked
comment: THE SECOND TABLE BUILDER (far 0x1CE:0x014D; the first is 0x22E0 = 0x1CE:0x0000). AX = a parameter, BX = the destination table, and it walks the LIVE PALETTE DS:0x5251 for cx=0x100 entries. Called once, at 0x9622, with ax=0xE0 (224) and bx=DS:0x6011 -- which is why 0x6011 is all-zero in the image and never appears as a `mov di` destination for 0x22E0: a different builder fills it. 224 is the base of the 16-colour CONSOLE BANK (224..239) the intro band's pixels all lie in, so this table plausibly remaps the screen INTO that bank; the montage's full-screen remap at 0x7ACE uses exactly this table. ALREADY LIFTED BIT-EXACTLY: recomp func_242d (oracle-verified) || SUPERSEDED READING `ds_es_rebase_gs`: helper prologue: bp=ax; ds=es=gs. Rebases the segment registers to the GS work arena before a data operation || MERGED 2026-07-25 (audit-fixes #131): the superseded rows were left in the file beside their own correction, so a reader who found one had no pointer to the other.

name: console_band_source
comment: THE INTRO MONTAGE'S CONSOLE BAND, identified: it is bridge-panorama frame 90's rows 140..200, pushed through the console-bank remap table DS:0x6011 (built by 0x242D with ax=0xE0). Proven by construction -- that composition equals the previously harvested accuracy/captures/console_band.idx in ALL 19200 bytes. The band was never separate art; it is the panorama colour-reduced by the montage's full-screen remap at 0x7AC3. Earlier attempts missed it by comparing the panorama's RAW indices (0..~75) with the band's POST-REMAP indices (224..239) and calling the ranges disjoint -- the transform was exactly what made them differ. PORTED: engine.rs overlay_console_band now composes from TB.BIG

name: nav_choice_handler_4_full
comment: HANDLER 4 FULL DECODE (dispatch-table entry 4). Phases: [0x2565]&1 -> reset [0xADB], query-only layout prepass ([0x27E6] bracket around 0x8428); [0x2565]&2 -> interpolate 0x2AAB toward 0x253D via 0x8B:0xFAD, `jae` exits while incomplete, else clear the phase. Then the real 0x8428 call returns the selection; a NEGATIVE value exits. The selection dispatch is a CHAIN of `dec al / jns`, not a jump table: sel 0 -> [0x259B]=[0x259C]=1; sel 1 -> gated on [0xADE]&1, toggles the tablo2 voc via [0xBA3]/[0xBA0] and swaps the target-list pointer; sel 2 -> [0x2738]=1,[0x2736]=1 (left); sel 3 -> [0x2738]=1,[0x2737]=1 (right); sel 4 -> [0xB13]=2,[0xA3E]=0,[0xA40]=0. Tail always clears [0x2A19] and bit2 of [0x2793]. VERIFIED against ship3d.rs run_ship_3d_nav_choice_handler_4 -- exact match including the fall-through past selection 4 || MERGED 2026-07-25 (audit-fixes #130), also recorded as: navigation-choice handler 4 (dispatch-table entry 4) -- the largest: target-list toggle DS:0x2567/0x2569 between DS:0x2578 and DS:0x2581, the mu\\tablo2.voc sound gate, and the left/right/motion latches DS:0x2736/0x2737/0x2738. PORTED: ship3d.rs run_ship_3d_nav_choice_handler_4 || five-way handler: menu gate, tablo2 VOC toggle, left/right motion gates, sound gate

name: save_name_edit_length
comment: the save-name edit LENGTH. NOT advanced by the edit routine 0x1DD8 -- the only writers in the image are `mov word [0x272E],0` at 0x1BF3 and the `inc` at 0x1C05 inside a scan that counts the buffer at DS:0x273B up to a NUL or a SPACE. So the length is RE-DERIVED by the surrounding flow between keystrokes, not maintained by the editor. A harness that calls 0x1DD8 alone keeps overwriting position 0

name: clip_top_not_width
comment: CLIP TOP (not a width). The string-draw entry 0x3192 guards with `cmp dx,gs:[0x523B] / ja` and `cx = gs:[0x5239]-8 / cmp dx,cx / jle`, and DX is the ROW -- 0x31BA..0x31C1 build the framebuffer offset as dx*320 + bx. So 0x5239/0x523B are the clip's TOP and BOTTOM, and BX is the column. Seeding them as width/height makes the routine bail before drawing anything (the 0x27CD accumulator comes back 0), which is how this was found

name: tint_table_builder_not_vertex_projection
comment: NAME CORRECTION for 0x22E0. Earlier passes called it `abs_negate_gs_setup` and, in src/recomp/ptr_leaves.rs, `3D-vertex projection ... writes one projected byte` -- both described the first four instructions and guessed the rest. It is the TINT REMAP-TABLE BUILDER: negate AX into a blend percent, prescale the target colour BX/CX/DX by /100, then walk the 256-entry palette at gs:0x5251 blending each entry toward the target and nearest-searching for the result, filling a 256-byte table at DI. Verified: the port's hand-written build_palette_blend_remap_table matches the lift ptr_leaves_gen::func_22e0 byte for byte over the real palette

name: capstone_prints_cbw_as_cwde
comment: TOOLING TRAP: opcode 0x98 here is architecturally CBW (sign-extend AL into AX), but re/tools/dis.py prints `cwde` because capstone renders 0x98 that way even in CS_MODE_16. Same for 0x99 (CWD, printed `cdq`). The distinction is semantic, not cosmetic: CWDE would leave AH holding whatever the caller left, so the D2 handler's stored value would depend on dispatcher state instead of the operand. tools/check_cited_instructions.py now treats cbw/cwde and cwd/cdq as equivalent so a correctly-spelled comment is not reported as wrong

name: remap_vclip_uses_xmax_bug
comment: ORIGINAL-GAME BUG (2026-07-25). The remap/window blit's clip ladder checks its VERTICAL extent against DS:0x5237 -- the HORIZONTAL RIGHT bound -- not DS:0x523B: `mov ax,cx / add ax,bp / sub ax,[0x5237]` where cx=y and bp=height. Every other clip ladder uses 0x523B for the bottom (0x9B04 point plot: x vs 0x5235/0x5237, y vs 0x5239/0x523B; string row draw 0x3437 `cmp dx,gs:[0x523B]`). It survived because right (320) > bottom (200), so the vertical clamp never fires for a rect that fits on screen. Consequence under a LETTERBOX window: the TOP bound is still honoured (0x33E2 pulls y down to [0x5239]) while the bottom is effectively open, so a tall tint runs past the letterbox floor. Ported verbatim in sprite::remap_rect_indexed_clipped with a discriminating test

name: render_xclip_hi
comment: clip RIGHT bound (x max). Paired with DS:0x5235 (left); 0x9B04 rejects a point with `cmp ax,[0x5237] / jge`. ALSO read as the vertical bound by the remap ladder at 0x33E6 -- see remap_vclip_uses_xmax_bug

name: station_record_table
comment: THE BRIDGE STATION RECORDS, static in the image at file 0xFE3B (2026-07-25). SIX records of 0x18 bytes: the walker at 0x7DAB is `mov bp,0x2A1B / mov cx,6 / test al,1 / test al,4 / ... / add bp,0x18 / loop 0x7DAE`, dispatching each record through `call word cs:[bx+0x6D4]`. 0x9642 clears the array the same way (`mov word [bp],0` x6). 0x985F fills +0xC..+0x1C with 0xFFFFFFFF (four words = the orb box). Field +0xA is the REST ANGLE IN DEGREES: records 0..5 = 0x000,0x05A,0x0B4,0x10E,0,0 at file 0xFE45/0xFE5D/0xFE75/0xFE8D. At 2 degrees per panorama frame that is frames 0,45,90,135 (helm, golden menu, pyramid nav room, organic Orxx). This REPLACES the port's earlier BRIDGEPROBE runtime dump as the source -- the bytes were static all along

name: station_record_stride
comment: `add bp,0x18` + `loop 0x7DAE` -- the station-record stride (24 bytes) and the 6-iteration walk over DS:0x2A1B. Field offsets confirmed against 0x985F (orb box at +0xC) and the static rest angles at +0xA

name: nav_choice_handler_2
comment: CONSOLE ROW 2 = THE CONTACT MENU, built from live state, never a fixed list: `mov si,0x6D3E / mov di,0x2B13`, then per word LODSW -- zero means EMPTY SLOT and is SKIPPED (`or ax,ax / je` loops back), 0xFFFF terminates and is stored, otherwise `add ax,4` + STOSW. Record+4 is the object's INLINE NAME (see vm.rs object_inline_name), so the menu is the names of whoever is aboard. Ported as VmMachine::ship_contact_menu_words with a test pinning skip/terminate/name || MERGED 2026-07-25 (audit-fixes #130), also recorded as: special-slot target handler: builds list from DS:0x6D3E, waits interpolation, sets deferred related and input gate || navigation-choice handler 2 (dispatch-table entry 2). PORTED: ship3d.rs run_ship_3d_nav_choice_handler_2

name: ship_slot_array
comment: THE 16-ENTRY SHIP-SLOT ARRAY (file 0x1415E, all zeros in the image -- runtime state). Walked with `mov cx,0x10` by the find scan at 0x5FD8, the second find/remove at 0x5FF6, and the free-slot scan at 0x6008 (`cmp word [bp],0 / je` = first empty slot). Consumed by the row-2 contact-menu build at 0x87BD. The port models it as VmMachine::ship_slots

name: option_menu_label_pointer_list
comment: THE BRIDGE OPTION MENU'S LABELS (2026-07-25), file 0x0F987. A 0xFFFF-terminated list of DS pointers to NUL-terminated strings, loaded by console row 4's handler 0x886C (`mov si,0x2567`) and drawn by the list widget at 0x8428. Entries: 0x2573 TEXT, 0x2581 MUSIC_OFF, 0x258B SAVE, 0x2590 LOAD, 0x2595 QUIT. MUSIC_ON at 0x2578 lies BETWEEN TEXT and MUSIC_OFF and is NOT in the pointer list -- it is the toggle's other face, swapped in by state. CANCEL is not here either: it is the widget's shared trailing entry at DS:0x0174. A further pointer list at DS:0x259D feeds the text-speed submenu (VERY FAST, ...). This REPLACES the port's hardcoded six-label list

name: option_menu_music_on_label
comment: `MUSIC_ON` -- the alternate face of the OPTION menu's music toggle. Absent from the DS:0x2567 pointer list (which names MUSIC_OFF) because the state swaps it in

name: dnsdb_drv_vector6_queue_buffer
comment: dnsdb.drv VECTOR 6 (driver file offset 0x0305, NOT a BLOODPRG address): takes a voice struct in si, les di,[si] = buffer, bx=[si+4] = length, terminates with mov byte es:[bx+di+6],0 @drv 0x336 and sets es:[di+2]=2. Confirms the 6-byte voice header from the OTHER binary. See re/tools/drv_vectors.py

name: croolis_camera_x_high_word
comment: CORRECTED (audit-fixes #271): NOT a standalone word. It is the HIGH WORD of the 32-bit accumulator at 0x22EA (`add dword ptr [0x22ea],eax` @0x1FC5). `movsx eax,word ptr [0x22ec]` @0xBFA reads a word because it wants the integer part, not because the storage is 16-bit. All three camera axes are accumulators: 0x22EA/0x22EE/0x22F2, read via 0x22EC/0x22F0/0x22F4.

name: croolis_camera_y_fixed
comment: Alien-view camera Y as a 32-BIT FIXED-POINT accumulator: `mov ecx,dword ptr [0x22ee]` @0x791, `add dword ptr [0x22ee],eax` @0x1FD5. The proximity test reads its HIGH WORD at [0x22f0] (0xA62), i.e. the integer part -- so a port storing this as an i16 loses the fractional motion (audit-fixes #269). | Sibling of 0x22EA and 0x22F2; each is stepped by [0x22d2|0x22d6|0x22da] * ebx >> 3 at 0x1FC2..0x1FE5.

name: ship_3d_temp_snd_viewport_descriptor_write
comment: builds the 16-byte viewport descriptor through the FAR POINTER at DS:0x522D: stosw 0 / inc ax / stosw 1 / add ax,3 / stosd 4 / stosw 0x140 / stosw 0xC8 / xor eax,eax / stosd 0. Values 0/1/4 are COMPUTED, not immediates -- no byte search or immediate scan can find this table (#288). The two stosd make words [3] and [7] HIGH HALVES, so the real shape is u16,u16,u32,u16,u16,u32, not eight fields. Ported: SHIP_3D_TEMP_SND_VIEWPORT_DESCRIPTOR

name: scene_blit_base_ten_row_setup
comment: THE THIRD SCENE BLIT BASE (audit-fixes #315/#316): builds a pointer into a 128-byte-stride table -- al=[0x6CDE] index, cbw, shl ax,7, add ax,0x1320, store [0x131A] -- copies [0x131E]->[0x131F], then sets the scene blit base gs:[0x1FA7]=0xA (ten rows) and [0x131C]=0 before jmp 0x7B80. The blit reads the base at 0xA464/0xAB6E (add bx,gs:[0x1fa7]). The port models only the 0x23 band top and the 0 full-screen bases, so this placement is MISSING; what selects this path is still undecoded -- the 0x1320 table and its [0x6CDE] index are the next step.

name: concept_list_show_setup
comment: IN-WINDOW CONCEPT-LIST show path (audit-fixes #324): or [0x2793],4 -- ANOTHER bit-2 setter, corroborating #311 that bit 2 means 'something is running, defer the pending-profile load' (the main-loop gate at 0x1095 tests bits 1|2|3); inc [0x67BA]; clears [0xADC]/[0xADD]/[0xADB]; sets the concept anchor [0xAC6]=0xE1 (centre-X 225) and [0xADA]=4, [0x27E6]=1 around call 0x8428. SI (the word-offset list) is INHERITED from this routine's caller, so the list identity is decided upstream -- that caller is what menu_submenu_labels must reach instead of its min_by_key proxy (docs/port-validation.md APPROX).

name: string_upcase_in_place
comment: IN-PLACE UPPER-CASE of a NUL-terminated string: mov al,es:[di] / cmp al,0x61 / jb skip / and al,0xdf / store / inc di / or al,al / jne. Characters BELOW 'a' are LEFT UNTOUCHED, so an underscore (0x5F) SURVIVES. CONTEXT CORRECTED (audit-fixes #328): this is NOT a callable helper -- 0 near callers, 0 far calls -- it is a fall-through block, and the instructions immediately before it are a DOS READ (int 21h AH=3Fh with the handle from gs:[0xA88]) followed by pop di / pop es. So it upper-cases something just LOADED FROM A FILE, most plausibly a path or name being normalised, and #327 was wrong to present it as the caption renderer's fold. The mechanical fact (0x5F preserved) stands; its relevance to PHONE_CONTACTS does not. Sibling fold at 0x77B5.

name: console_mode_dismiss_ladder
comment: CONSOLE-MODE DISMISS ladder (audit-fixes #337): `dec al / jns` arms selected by AL -- arm0 sets [0x2738]=1 and [0x2736]=1 (INPUT_GATE_E), arm1 sets [0x2738]=1 and [0x2737]=1 (INPUT_GATE_F), arm2 sets [0xB13]=2 and clears [0xA3E]/[0xA40]. COMMON TAIL at 0x8956: `mov word [0x2a19],0` clears INPUT_GATE_I, then `and byte [0x2793],0xfb` @0x895C clears the busy bit 2 -- a THIRD clear site beside 0x59BF and 0x5E99. So the gate flags 0x2736/0x2737 are raised per console MODE while the busy bit is dropped on dismissal, which is what the main-loop gate at 0x1095 reads to decide whether a pending script profile may load.

name: console_menu_pick_dispatch
comment: CONSOLE MENU PICK -> MODE DISPATCH (audit-fixes #338). `mov byte [0x2565],0` clears INPUT_GATE_D, then `push cs / call 0x8428` runs the unified list widget (list_widget_layout_unified) and `or ax,ax / js` rejects a negative (no pick). AL then falls through a FIVE-ARM `dec al / jns` ladder at 0x88C3 / 0x88D4 / 0x8923 / 0x8933 / 0x8943 -- one arm per MENU ROW -- each raising that mode subsystem flag ([0x2736] and [0x2737] are arms 2 and 3, alongside the shared [0x2738]). Common tail 0x8956 clears [0x2A19] and the busy bit `and [0x2793],0xfb` @0x895C. SO AL IS THE PICKED ROW INDEX: the console-mode flags the main-loop gate (0x1095) reads are set by the row the player chose, and the row ORDER comes from the widget word-offset list in SI -- the same list identity docs/port-validation.md records as unresolved for menu_submenu_labels.

name: console_menu_list_pointer_setup
comment: CONSOLE MENU list pointer, UNRESOLVED (audit-fixes #339, retracted in #340). `mov si,0x2AAB / mov di,0x25CF / movsd / movsd` copies 8 bytes AND ADVANCES SI BY 8; the push si @0x88A3 / pop si @0x88AF around the lcall preserve the ADVANCED value, and no `mov si` follows, so SI at the call to list_widget_layout_unified @0x88BA traces to 0x2AB3. BUT 0x2AB3 IS THE WIDGET'S OWN WIDTH SCRATCH -- its only three references are inside the widget (0x844E, 0x8493, 0x854E) and nothing external ever writes a row list there. Both facts are checked and they do not fit: either the trace misses a write to SI, or this call site uses the widget in a mode where SI is already the width buffer. DO NOT record either reading as the list source until that is settled. The real lesson here is the movsd advance: reading back to the nearest `mov si,imm16` gives 0x2AAB, which is definitely wrong.

name: bridge_view_sector_update
comment: BRIDGE VIEW SECTOR -> the HIGH NIBBLE of gs:0x2793 (audit-fixes #364). `mov ax,[0x2793] / and ax,0xff0f` clears bits 4-7, then `test ax,2 / jne 0x9544` SKIPS the recompute when bit 1 is set -- bit 1 is a LOCK, which is why no memory-form test of it exists (the test is on the register). Otherwise bx is stepped by the panorama frame [0x2795]: frame<=0x16 or >0x9D -> 1; <=0x43 -> 2; <=0x70 -> 4; else 8, then `shl bx,4 / or ax,bx / mov [0x2793],ax`. So bits 4..7 are a ONE-HOT QUADRANT of the 180-frame (2deg) panorama -- boundaries 22/67/112/157 are the four 90deg sectors -- NOT independent flags. This is why the census (#358) found them read with masks 0x10/0x20/0x40/0x50/0x90 but never OR-set: they are computed, not raised.
